title.zh: 卷三十六 列傳第二十六 羊欣 羊玄保 沈演之 江夷 江秉之
title.en: Volume 36 Biographies 26: Yang Xin, Yang Xuanbao, Shen Yanzhi, Jiangyi, Jiang Bingzhi
title.raw: 卷三十六 列傳第二十六 羊欣 羊玄保 沈演之 江夷 江秉之 Volume 36 Biographies 26: Yang Xin, Yang Xuanbao, Shen Yanzhi, Jiangyi, Jiang Bingzhi

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十六

translations.literal: Biographies 26
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Number Twenty-Six

sentences.zh: 羊欣羊玄保沈演之江夷江秉之

translations.literal: Yang Xin, Yang Xuanbao, Shen Yanzhi, Jiang Yi, and Jiang Bingzhi
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xin · Yang Xuanbao · Shen Yanzhi · Jiang Yi · Jiang Bingzhi

sentences.zh: 羊欣，字敬元，泰山南城人也。

translations.literal: Yang Xin, styled Jingyuan, was a man of Nancheng in Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xin, whose courtesy name was Jingyuan, came from Nancheng in Mount Tai commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖忱，晋徐州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Chen was Jin Inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chen had served as Inspector of Xu Province under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 祖权，黄门郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Quan was a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Quan held the post of Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 父不疑，桂阳太守。

translations.literal: His father Buyi was Administrator of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Buyi served as Administrator of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 欣少靖默，無競于人，美言笑，善容止。

translations.literal: From youth Xin was quiet and reserved, contending with no one; he spoke gracefully and carried himself well.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth Xin was serene and unobtrusive, never competing with others; his conversation was pleasing and his bearing elegant.

sentences.zh: 泛覽經籍，尤長隸書。

translations.literal: He read widely in the classics and was especially skilled in clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged broadly through the classics and excelled above all in clerical script calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 父不疑為烏程令，欣年十二。

translations.literal: When his father Buyi was magistrate of Wucheng, Xin was twelve.
translations.idiomatic: His father Buyi was serving as magistrate of Wucheng when Xin was twelve years old.

sentences.zh: 時王獻之為吳興太守，甚知愛之。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Xianzhi was Administrator of Wu Commandery and came to know and love him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianzhi was then Administrator of Wu Commandery and took a keen liking to the boy.

sentences.zh: 欣嘗夏月著新絹裙晝寢，獻之入縣見之，書裙數幅而去。

translations.literal: Once in summer Xin wore a new silk skirt and napped by day; Xianzhi entered the county office, saw him, wrote several lines on the skirt, and left.
translations.idiomatic: One summer day Xin napped in a new silk skirt; Xianzhi came into the county hall, saw him asleep, wrote several lines of calligraphy on the skirt, and departed.

sentences.zh: 欣書本工，因此彌善。

translations.literal: Xin's writing was already accomplished, and through this it became still better.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's hand was already accomplished; this incident pushed his skill still further.

sentences.zh: 起家輔國參軍，府解還家。

translations.literal: He first entered office as an aide in the Army That Supports the State, then left when the office was dissolved and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as an aide in the Army That Supports the State; when that command was dissolved he went home.

sentences.zh: 隆安中，朝廷漸亂，欣優遊私門，不復進仕。

translations.literal: In the Long'an era the court grew increasingly chaotic; Xin lived at ease in private life and no longer sought advancement.
translations.idiomatic: During the Long'an reign the court slid into disorder, and Xin withdrew into private life, refusing further office.

sentences.zh: 會稽王世子元顯每使書扇，常不奉命。

translations.literal: The Prince of Kuaiji's son Yuanxian often sent for him to write on fans, and he regularly refused the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian, son of the Prince of Kuaiji, repeatedly ordered him to inscribe folding fans, and Xin routinely declined.

sentences.zh: 元顯怒，乃以為其後軍府舍人。

translations.literal: Yuanxian grew angry and made him a clerk in the Rear Army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Yuanxian forced him into a clerkship in the Rear Army headquarters.

sentences.zh: 此職本用寒人，欣意貌恬然，不以高卑見色，論者稱焉。

translations.literal: This post was normally filled by men of humble birth; Xin's expression remained calm and he showed no change of color over high or low rank, and commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The post was meant for men of humble birth, yet Xin's face stayed untroubled and he betrayed no resentment at the demotion; observers praised his composure.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣領軍謝混，混拂席改服然後見之。

translations.literal: Once he went to call on the Commander of the Central Army, Xie Hun, who brushed off his seat and changed his clothes before receiving him.
translations.idiomatic: On one visit to Commander of the Central Army Xie Hun, Hun swept his mat and changed garments before admitting him.

sentences.zh: 時混族子靈運在坐，退告族兄瞻曰：「望蔡見羊欣，遂改席易衣。

translations.literal: At the time Hun's clansman Lingyun was present; on withdrawing he told his elder clansman Zhan, "When Wang Cai saw Yang Xin, he changed his seat and clothes."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun, a clansman of Hun's, was present; leaving, he told his elder kinsman Zhan, "The moment Wang Cai saw Yang Xin he rearranged his seat and changed his clothes."

sentences.zh: 」欣由此益知名。

translations.literal: From this Xin became still more renowned.
translations.idiomatic: After that episode Xin's fame spread further.

sentences.zh: 桓玄輔政，以欣為平西主簿，參豫機要。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan held the government, he made Xin chief clerk of the Pacifying West headquarters and had him join in confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan directed the government, he appointed Xin chief clerk on the Pacifying West staff and brought him into confidential deliberations.

sentences.zh: 欣欲自疏，時漏密事。

translations.literal: Xin wished to keep his distance, and at times leaked secret matters.
translations.idiomatic: Xin wanted to distance himself and occasionally let confidential matters slip.

sentences.zh: 玄覺其此意，愈更重之，以為楚台殿中郎。

translations.literal: Xuan perceived this intention and valued him all the more, appointing him Palace Gentleman of the Chu Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan saw what he was doing and prized him still more highly, making him Palace Gentleman of the Chu Terrace.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「尚書政事之本，殿中禮樂所出。

translations.literal: He said to him, "The Secretariat is the root of government affairs; the Palace is where ritual and music proceed.
translations.idiomatic: "The Secretariat is the root of state business," he told him, "and the Palace is where ritual and music originate.

sentences.zh: 卿昔處股肱，方此為輕。

translations.literal: You once stood at the ruler's right hand; compared with that, this is light duty."
translations.idiomatic: You once served at the ruler's right hand—this post is lighter by comparison."

sentences.zh: 」欣就職少日，稱病自免，屏居裏巷十餘年。

translations.literal: Xin took office for only a few days, then pleaded illness and resigned, living in seclusion in his lane for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Xin held the post only a few days before pleading illness and resigning; he then lived in seclusion in his neighborhood for more than a decade.

sentences.zh: 義熙中，弟徽被知于武帝，帝謂諮議參軍鄭鮮之曰：「羊徽一時美器，世論猶在兄後。

translations.literal: In the Yixi era his younger brother Hui came to the notice of Emperor Wu, who said to Adviser Zheng Xianzhi, "Yang Hui is a fine vessel of the age, yet public opinion still ranks him below his elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: During the Yixi reign his brother Hui caught Emperor Wu's eye; the emperor told Adviser Zheng Xianzhi, "Yang Hui is a treasure of our time, yet opinion still places him beneath his elder brother."

sentences.zh: 」即板欣補右軍劉藩司馬。

translations.literal: He immediately issued a provisional appointment making Xin acting marshal of the Right Army under Liu Fan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once issued a provisional order appointing Xin acting marshal on Right Army commander Liu Fan's staff.

sentences.zh: 後為新安太守，在郡四年，簡惠著稱。

translations.literal: Later he became Administrator of Xin'an and, in four years in the commandery, won renown for simplicity and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Administrator of Xin'an; in four years there he earned a reputation for simple, benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 除臨川王義慶輔國長史，廬陵王義真車騎諮議參軍，並不就。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Aide to the Army That Supports the State under Prince of Linchuan Yiqing and Military Adviser to the Chariots and Cavalry under Prince of Luling Yizhen, but accepted neither post.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered chief aide to Prince of Linchuan Yiqing's Army That Supports the State and military adviser on Prince of Luling Yizhen's chariot-and-cavalry staff, but declined both.

sentences.zh: 文帝重以為新安太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen again appointed him Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once more made him Administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 在郡十三年，樂其山水，嘗謂子弟曰：「人生仕宦至二千石，斯可矣。

translations.literal: In thirteen years in the commandery he delighted in its mountains and waters, and once told his sons and nephews, "In life, reaching the rank of two-thousand-bushel official is enough."
translations.idiomatic: He spent thirteen years in the commandery, loving its landscape, and once told his sons and nephews, "In this life, reaching a two-thousand-bushel post is sufficient."

sentences.zh: 」及是便懷止足。

translations.literal: At that point he felt content to stop.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he felt he had reached enough.

sentences.zh: 轉義興太守，非其好也。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Yixing, which was not to his liking.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Administrator of Yixing—a post he did not want.

sentences.zh: 頃之，稱病篤免歸。

translations.literal: Before long he pleaded grave illness and was dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he pleaded grave illness, resigned, and went home.

sentences.zh: 除中散大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Master of Palace Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as Grand Master of Palace Leisure.

sentences.zh: 素好黃、老，常手自書章。

translations.literal: He had long favored Huang-Lao teachings and often copied ritual texts by hand.
translations.idiomatic: He had long favored Huang-Lao teachings and often copied talismanic texts in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 有病不服藥，飲符水而已。

translations.literal: When ill he took no medicine and drank only talisman water.
translations.idiomatic: When ill he refused medicine and drank only consecrated talisman water.

sentences.zh: 兼善醫術，撰藥方數十卷。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in medicine and compiled several tens of volumes of prescriptions.
translations.idiomatic: He was also versed in medicine and compiled several dozen scrolls of medical formulas.

sentences.zh: 欣以不堪拜伏，辭不朝覲，自非尋省近親，不妄行詣。

translations.literal: Because he could not bear to bow and prostrate himself, he declined court audience; except when visiting close kin nearby he would not go out casually.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to endure bowing and prostration, he excused himself from court audiences and would not go out casually except to visit close kin nearby.

sentences.zh: 行必由城外，未嘗入六門。

translations.literal: When he went out he always took the road outside the walls and never entered the six gates.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he traveled he kept to roads outside the city walls and never passed through the six gates.

sentences.zh: 武帝、文帝並恨不識之。

translations.literal: Emperors Wu and Wen both regretted never having known him.
translations.idiomatic: Both Emperor Wu and Emperor Wen regretted that they had never met him in person.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十九年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the nineteenth year of Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the nineteenth year of the Yuanjia era.

sentences.zh: 弟徽字敬猷，時譽多欣，位河東太守，卒。

translations.literal: His younger brother Hui, styled Jingyou, was more praised in the age than Xin; he reached the post of Administrator of Hedong and died.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Hui, courtesy name Jingyou, outshone Xin in contemporary reputation; he rose to Administrator of Hedong and died in office.

sentences.zh: 羊玄保，泰山南城人也。

translations.literal: Yang Xuanbao was a man of Nancheng in Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuanbao came from Nancheng in Mount Tai commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖楷，晉尚書都官郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kai was Jin Director of the Ministry of Justice in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kai had been Director of the Ministry of Justice in the Jin Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父綏，中書侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Sui was Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sui served as a Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 玄保初為宋武帝鎮軍參軍，少帝景平中，累遷司徒右長史。

translations.literal: Xuanbao first served as an aide in Emperor Wu of Song's Pacifying Army; in the Jingping era of Emperor Shao he was promoted step by step to Senior Aide of the Right in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbao began as an aide on Emperor Wu of Song's Pacifying Army staff; under Emperor Shao, in the Jingping era, he rose by stages to Senior Aide of the Right in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 府公王弘甚知重之，謂左長史庾登之、吏部尚書王准之曰：「卿二賢明美朗詣，會悟多通，然弘懿之望，故當共推羊也。

translations.literal: The Secretariat chief Wang Hong knew and valued him greatly, and said to Senior Aide of the Left Yu Dengzhi and Minister of Personnel Wang Zhunzhi, "You two are brilliant, clear, and broadly accomplished, yet in the expectation of steady virtue you should together defer to Yang."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong, chief of the Secretariat, prized him highly and told Senior Aide of the Left Yu Dengzhi and Minister of Personnel Wang Zhunzhi, "You are both brilliant and broadly capable, yet when it comes to steady, deep virtue you should yield pride of place to Yang."

sentences.zh: 」頃之，入為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he entered court as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he entered the capital as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 善弈棋，品第三。

translations.literal: He was skilled at weiqi and ranked third in grade.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at weiqi and was graded third in the official rankings of players.

sentences.zh: 文帝亦好弈，與賭郡，玄保戲勝，以補宣城太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen also loved the game and wagered commanderies with him; Xuanbao won in jest and was appointed Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen also loved weiqi and once wagered commanderies on the board; Xuanbao won in sport and was appointed Administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 先是劉式之為宣城立吏人亡叛制，一人不禽，符伍裏吏送州作部；

translations.literal: Earlier Liu Shizhi as Administrator of Xuancheng had established a system for clerks regarding fugitives: if one man was not captured, the whole ward of clerks was sent to the province for corvée labor;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as Administrator of Xuancheng, Liu Shizhi had imposed a clerk-liability rule for fugitives: if even one man escaped capture, every clerk in the ward was sent to provincial corvée;

sentences.zh: 能禽者賞位二階。

translations.literal: whoever captured one received promotion of two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: whoever captured a fugitive was rewarded with a two-rank promotion.

sentences.zh: 玄保以為非宜，陳之曰：「臣伏尋亡叛之由，皆出於窮逼。

translations.literal: Xuanbao thought this unsuitable and memorialized, saying, "Your servant has examined the causes of flight and finds they all arise from desperate poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbao judged the rule unsound and memorialized: "I have traced the causes of flight and find they stem from desperate poverty.

sentences.zh: 今立殊制，於事為苦。

translations.literal: Now to establish an exceptional system makes governance bitter.
translations.idiomatic: To impose so harsh an exceptional rule only deepens the hardship of governance.

sentences.zh: 又尋此制施一邦而已，若其是邪，則應與天下為一；

translations.literal: Further, this system applies to one commandery alone; if it is right, it should be one with the whole realm;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover this measure applies to one commandery alone; if it is right, it should bind the whole realm equally;

sentences.zh: 若其非邪，亦不宜獨行一郡。

translations.literal: if it is wrong, it should not be enforced in a single commandery alone."
translations.idiomatic: if it is wrong, it should not be enforced in one commandery by itself."

sentences.zh: 」由此制停。

translations.literal: Because of this the system was halted.
translations.idiomatic: On this basis the system was abolished.

sentences.zh: 曆丹陽尹，會稽太守，太常，吳郡太守。

translations.literal: He served as Prefect of Danyang, Administrator of Kuaiji, Grand Minister of Ceremonies, and Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Prefect of Danyang, Administrator of Kuaiji, Grand Minister of Ceremonies, and Administrator of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 文帝以玄保廉素寡欲，故頻授名郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, because Xuanbao was frugal and of few desires, repeatedly gave him famous commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xuanbao lived frugally and desired little, Emperor Wen repeatedly posted him to prestigious commanderies.

sentences.zh: 為政雖無殊績，而去後常必見思。

translations.literal: Though his governance showed no special achievement, after he left people always missed him.
translations.idiomatic: His administration produced no spectacular feats, yet after each departure the people always missed him.

sentences.zh: 不營財利，產業儉薄。

translations.literal: He did not pursue wealth and his estate remained modest.
translations.idiomatic: He never pursued profit, and his household remained spare.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘗曰：「人仕宦非唯須才，亦須運命。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen once said, "In taking office one needs not only talent but also fate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once remarked, "Office requires not only talent but also fortune.

sentences.zh: 每有好官缺，我未嘗不先憶羊玄保。

translations.literal: Whenever a good post fell vacant I never failed to think first of Yang Xuanbao."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a fine post opened, I never failed to think first of Yang Xuanbao."

sentences.zh: 」元凶弑立，以為吏部尚書，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince assassin seized the throne, he made Xuanbao Minister of Personnel and concurrent Director of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: When the assassin prince seized the throne, he appointed Xuanbao Minister of Personnel and concurrent Director of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 及孝武入伐，朝士多南奔，劭集群僚，橫刀怒曰：「卿等便可去矣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu marched in to punish him, many court officials fled south; the assassin assembled the officials, drew his sword in anger, and said, "You may all leave now."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu marched east to punish the usurper, many courtiers fled south; the usurper gathered his officials, bared his sword, and snarled, "You may all go now."

sentences.zh: 」眾並懼莫敢言。

translations.literal: All were afraid and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Terror silenced the hall; no one dared reply.

sentences.zh: 玄保容色不異，徐曰：「臣其以死奉朝。

translations.literal: Xuanbao's expression did not change, and he said slowly, "Your servant will serve the dynasty with his death."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbao's face never changed; calmly he said, "I shall serve the dynasty with my life."

sentences.zh: 」劭為解。

translations.literal: The assassin relented.
translations.idiomatic: The usurper softened and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，為金紫光祿大夫，以謹敬見知。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Xuanbao became Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle and was known for careful respect.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu ascended, Xuanbao became Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, esteemed for his careful reverence.

sentences.zh: 大明五年，加散騎常侍、特進。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daming he was given the additional titles of Regular Attendant and Special Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daming he received the additional titles of Regular Attendant and Special Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 玄保自少至老，謹於祭奠，四時珍新未得祠薦者，口不妄嘗。

translations.literal: From youth to old age Xuanbao was scrupulous in sacrifice; seasonal delicacies not yet offered at the ancestral rites he would not taste at random.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to old age Xuanbao was meticulous in sacrifice; he would not casually taste seasonal delicacies until they had been offered at the ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰定子。

translations.literal: When he died he was given the posthumous title Dingzi.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he received the posthumous title Dingzi.

sentences.zh: 子戎少有才氣，而輕薄少行檢，語好為雙聲。

translations.literal: His son Rong had talent and spirit in youth but was frivolous and lacking in restraint, and in speech loved paired alliterative phrases.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rong showed talent and spirit in youth but was frivolous and ill-disciplined, delighting in paired alliterative phrases when he spoke.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭嘗設齋，使戎布床，須臾王出，以床狹，乃自開床。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiangxia Yigong once set out a vegetarian feast and had Rong arrange the couches; before long the prince came out, found the couches too narrow, and opened them himself.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jiangxia Yigong once held a vegetarian feast and ordered Rong to lay out the couches; when the prince emerged he found them too narrow and spread them wider himself.

sentences.zh: 戎曰：「官家恨狹，更廣八分，」王笑曰：「卿豈唯善雙聲，乃辯士也，」文帝好與玄保棋，嘗中使至，玄保曰：「今日上何召我邪？

translations.literal: Rong said, "The lord's seat resents narrowness—eight tenths wider," and the prince laughed, "You are not only good at paired sounds but a debater too." Emperor Wen loved playing weiqi with Xuanbao; once an imperial messenger arrived and Xuanbao said, "Why has His Majesty summoned me today?"
translations.idiomatic: Rong quipped, "The lord's seat resents narrowness—make it eight tenths wider." The prince laughed: "You are not only a master of paired sounds but a true debater." Emperor Wen loved playing weiqi with Xuanbao; once an imperial messenger arrived and Xuanbao asked, "Why has His Majesty summoned me today?"

sentences.zh: 「戎曰：「金溝清泚，銅池搖揚，既佳光景，當得劇棋。

translations.literal: Rong said, "The golden ditch runs clear and bright, the bronze pool sways and ripples—such fine scenery calls for a fierce game."
translations.idiomatic: Rong answered, "The golden ditch runs clear, the bronze pool shimmers—such splendid scenery demands a fierce game."

sentences.zh: 」玄保常嫌其輕脫，云：「此兒必亡我家」。

translations.literal: Xuanbao often resented his levity and said, "This boy will surely ruin my house."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbao often deplored his son's levity and said, "This boy will destroy our house."

sentences.zh: 位通直郎，坐與王僧達謗時政賜死。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Attendant of Direct Communication and was sentenced to death for slandering current affairs with Wang Sengda.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Attendant of Direct Communication but was sentenced to death for slandering current affairs together with Wang Sengda.

sentences.zh: 死後，孝武帝引見玄保，玄保謝曰：「臣無日磾之明，以此上負。

translations.literal: After Rong's death Emperor Xiaowu summoned Xuanbao, and Xuanbao apologized, saying, "Your servant lacks the clear sight of Ri Di and has failed in this duty above."
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's execution Emperor Xiaowu received Xuanbao, who apologized: "I lack Ri Di's clear judgment and have failed you in this."

sentences.zh: 」上美其言。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his reply.

sentences.zh: 戎二弟，文帝並賜名曰咸、曰粲，謂玄保曰：「欲令卿二子有林下正始餘風。」

translations.literal: Rong's two younger brothers were both given names by Emperor Wen—Xian and Can—and the emperor told Xuanbao, "I wish your two sons to carry something of the forest grace of the Zhengshi era."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen personally named Rong's two younger brothers Xian and Can, telling Xuanbao, "I want your two sons to preserve a trace of the reclusive Zhengshi spirit."

sentences.zh: 玄保既善棋，而何尚之亦雅好其事。

translations.literal: Xuanbao was skilled at weiqi, and He Shangzhi also loved the game.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbao excelled at weiqi, as did He Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 吳郡褚胤年七歲便入高品，及長，冠絕當時。

translations.literal: Chu Yin of Wu Commandery at seven entered the upper grade, and when grown he stood above all of his time.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yin of Wu Commandery entered the upper player grade at seven, and in adulthood stood unmatched in his generation.

sentences.zh: 胤父榮期與臧質同逆，胤應從誅。

translations.literal: Yin's father Rongqi joined Zang Zhi in rebellion, and Yin should have been executed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's father Rongqi joined Zang Zhi's rebellion, and Yin should have died by association.

sentences.zh: 何尚之固請曰：「胤弈棋之妙，超古冠今。

translations.literal: He Shangzhi firmly petitioned, saying, "Yin's skill at weiqi surpasses the ancients and crowns the present age.
translations.idiomatic: He Shangzhi petitioned urgently: "Yin's weiqi surpasses antiquity and crowns the present age.

sentences.zh: 魏犨犯令，以材獲免，父戮子宥，其例甚多。

translations.literal: Wei Chou violated orders yet was spared for his talent; fathers executed and sons pardoned have many precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chou broke the law yet was spared for talent; many precedents spare sons when fathers are executed.

sentences.zh: 特乞與其微命，使異術不絕。

translations.literal: I beg only that his humble life be spared so that this singular art not perish."
translations.idiomatic: I beg only that his life be spared so this singular art may not die."

sentences.zh: 」不許，時人痛惜之。

translations.literal: Permission was not granted, and people of the time grieved for it.
translations.idiomatic: The plea was denied, and contemporaries mourned the loss.

sentences.zh: 玄保兄子希字泰聞，少有才氣，為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Xuanbao's elder brother's son Xi, styled Tairong, had talent and spirit in youth and became Left Assistant Director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbao's nephew Xi, courtesy name Tairong, showed talent in youth and rose to Left Assistant Director in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時揚州刺史西陽王子尚上言：「山湖之禁，雖有舊科，人俗相因，替而不奉，熂山封水，保為家利。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Xiyang Zishang submitted a memorial: "The old statutes on mountains and lakes, though long established, have been ignored through custom; people seal hills and waters for private profit.
translations.idiomatic: Then Prince of Xiyang Zishang memorialized: "Statutes on mountains and lakes, though ancient, have fallen into neglect through custom; the powerful seal hills and waters for private gain.

sentences.zh: 自頃以來，頹弛日甚，富強者兼嶺而占，貧弱者薪蘇無托，至漁采之地亦又如茲。

translations.literal: In recent times the decay grows daily worse: the rich occupy whole ranges, the poor have no firewood or kindling, and even fishing and gathering lands are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the decay worsens daily: the wealthy seize whole ranges while the poor lack firewood; even fishing and foraging grounds suffer the same abuse.

sentences.zh: 斯實害人之深弊，為政所宜去絕。

translations.literal: This is truly a deep harm to the people and what governance should abolish.
translations.idiomatic: This is a grave injury to the people and what good governance must uproot.

sentences.zh: 損益舊條，更申恒制。

translations.literal: Revise the old articles and reassert a constant system."
translations.idiomatic: Revise the old statutes and restore a stable rule."

sentences.zh: 」有司檢壬辰詔書：「占山護澤，強盜律論。

translations.literal: The relevant offices examined the renchen edict of the second year of Xiankang: "Those who seize mountains and guard marshes are judged under the bandit law.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices reviewed the renchen edict of Xiankang year two: "Those who seize mountains and guard marshes are judged under the bandit statute.

sentences.zh: 贓一丈以上皆棄市。

translations.literal: Booty of one zhang or more is punished by execution and public display."
translations.idiomatic: Any booty of one zhang or more brought execution and public display."

sentences.zh: 」希以「壬辰之制，其禁嚴刻，事既難遵，理與時弛。

translations.literal: Xi argued that "the renchen regulation was severe and hard to obey, its principle already out of step with the times;
translations.idiomatic: Xi argued that "the renchen rule was harsh and impracticable, already out of step with the times;

sentences.zh: 而占山封水，漸染復滋，更相因仍，便成先業。

translations.literal: yet seizure of mountains and sealing of waters grows ever worse through repeated practice and has become established custom.
translations.idiomatic: yet seizure of hills and waters grows worse through repeated practice and has hardened into custom.

sentences.zh: 一朝頓去，易致嗟怨。

translations.literal: To abolish it all at once would easily provoke resentment."
translations.idiomatic: To abolish it all at once would provoke widespread resentment."

sentences.zh: 今更刊革，立制五條：凡是山澤先恒熂臑爐，養種竹木雜果為林艿，及陂湖江海魚梁鮆場，恒加功修作者，聽不追奪。

translations.literal: Now revise and establish five articles: all hills, marshes, former constant burning grounds, bamboo and fruit groves, dykes, lakes, rivers, seas, fish weirs, and oyster beds under constant cultivation and repair shall not be reclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed five revised articles: hills and marshes under long-standing cultivation—burned clearings, bamboo and fruit groves, dykes, lakes, rivers, seas, fish weirs, and oyster beds under constant upkeep—would not be seized back.

sentences.zh: 官品第一第二聽占山三頃；

translations.literal: Officials of ranks one and two may occupy three qing of mountain;
translations.idiomatic: Officials of ranks one and two might occupy three qing of mountain land;

sentences.zh: 第三第四品二頃五十畝；

translations.literal: ranks three and four, two qing fifty mu;
translations.idiomatic: ranks three and four, two qing and fifty mu;

sentences.zh: 第五第六品二頃；

translations.literal: ranks five and six, two qing;
translations.idiomatic: ranks five and six were allotted two qing;

sentences.zh: 第七第八品一頃五十畝；

translations.literal: ranks seven and eight, one qing fifty mu;
translations.idiomatic: ranks seven and eight, one qing and fifty mu;

sentences.zh: 第九品及百姓一頃：皆依定格，條上貲簿。

translations.literal: rank nine and commoners, one qing: all according to fixed quotas, entered on the property register.
translations.idiomatic: rank nine and commoners, one qing—all by fixed quota, recorded on the property register.

sentences.zh: 若先已占山，不得更占；

translations.literal: If one has already occupied mountain land, one may not occupy more;
translations.idiomatic: Those who already held mountain land could not add new claims;

sentences.zh: 先占闕少，依限占足。

translations.literal: if prior occupation falls short, one may fill to the limit.
translations.idiomatic: if prior holdings fell short, they might fill to the quota.

sentences.zh: 若非前條舊業，一不得禁。

translations.literal: If it is not an old holding under the prior articles, none may be seized.
translations.idiomatic: Holdings outside these prior categories could not be seized.

sentences.zh: 有犯者，水土一尺以上，並計贓依常盜律論。

translations.literal: Violators, for water or land of one chi or more, shall have booty calculated and be judged under the ordinary theft law.
translations.idiomatic: Violators, for encroachments of one chi or more on water or land, would have booty calculated and be judged under ordinary theft law.

sentences.zh: 停除咸康二年壬辰之科。

translations.literal: Abolish the renchen regulation of the second year of Xiankang."
translations.idiomatic: The Xiankang year-two renchen regulation would be abolished."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 時益州刺史劉瑀先為右衛將軍，與府司馬何季穆共事不平，季穆為尚書令建平王宏所親待，屢毀瑀於宏。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yu, Inspector of Yi Province, had earlier been General of the Right Guard and had worked poorly with headquarters marshal He Jimu; Jimu was favored by Minister of Personnel Prince of Jianping Hong, who repeatedly slandered Yu to Hong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Yu of Yi Province had earlier served as General of the Right Guard and clashed with headquarters marshal He Jimu; Jimu enjoyed Prince of Jianping Hong's favor as Minister of Personnel, and Hong heard repeated slanders against Yu.

sentences.zh: 會瑀出為益州，奪士人妻為妾，宏使希舉察之，瑀坐免官。

translations.literal: When Yu went out as Inspector of Yi Province and seized a scholar's wife as concubine, Hong had Xi investigate; Yu was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu went out as Inspector of Yi Province and seized a scholar's wife as concubine, Hong had Xi investigate and Yu was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 瑀恨希切齒，有門生謝元伯往來希間，瑀密令訪訊被免之由，希曰：「此奏非我意。

translations.literal: Yu hated Xi to the teeth; a disciple, Xie Yuanbo, moved between Xi's circle, and Yu secretly had him inquire why he had been dismissed; Xi said, "This memorial was not my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Yu hated Xi bitterly; his disciple Xie Yuanbo frequented Xi's circle, and Yu secretly asked why he had been dismissed; Xi said, "That memorial was not my intent."

sentences.zh: 」瑀即日到宏門奉箋陳謝，云：「聞之羊希。

translations.literal: Yu went the same day to Hong's gate with a written apology, saying, "I heard this from Yang Xi."
translations.idiomatic: That same day Yu went to Hong's gate with a written apology, saying, "I heard this from Yang Xi."

sentences.zh: 」希坐漏泄免官。

translations.literal: Xi was dismissed for leaking secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was dismissed for leaking confidential matters.

sentences.zh: 泰始三年，為甯朔將軍、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi he became General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi year three he was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 四年，希以沛郡劉思道行晉康太守，領軍伐俚。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Xi had Liu Sidao of Pei Commandery act as Administrator of Jinkang and lead the army against the Li tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Xi had Liu Sidao of Pei Commandery serve as acting Administrator of Jinkang and lead troops against the Li tribes.

sentences.zh: 思道違節失利，希遣收之。

translations.literal: Sidao disobeyed orders and failed; Xi sent men to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao broke orders and failed; Xi sent men to take him.

sentences.zh: 思道不受命，率所領襲州，希踰城走，思道獲而殺之。

translations.literal: Sidao refused the order, led his troops in a surprise attack on the province, Xi fled over the wall, and Sidao captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao refused, led his troops in a surprise attack on the provincial seat, Xi fled over the wall, and Sidao captured and killed him.

sentences.zh: 希子崇字伯遠，尚書主客郎，丁母憂，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: Xi's son Chong, styled Boyuan, was Director of Receptions in the Secretariat; when mourning his mother he exceeded ritual in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's son Chong, courtesy name Boyuan, was Director of Receptions in the Secretariat; mourning his mother, he exceeded ritual in grief.

sentences.zh: 及聞廣州亂，即日便徒跣出新亭，不能步涉，頓伏江渚。

translations.literal: When he heard of the turmoil in Guang Province he went the same day barefoot from Xinting; unable to walk across water, he collapsed on the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the turmoil in Guang Province, he went barefoot that same day from Xinting; unable to ford the water, he collapsed on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 門義以小船致之，父葬畢，乃不勝哀而卒。

translations.literal: A household retainer brought him in a small boat; after his father's burial he died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: A household retainer brought him in by small boat; after his father's burial he died of grief.

sentences.zh: 沈演之字台真，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Yanzhi, styled Taizhen, was a man of Wukang in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yanzhi, courtesy name Taizhen, came from Wukang in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖充，晉車騎將軍、吳國內史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Chong was Jin General of Chariots and Cavalry and Interior Minister of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chong had been Jin General of Chariots and Cavalry and Interior Minister of Wu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖勁，冠軍陳佑長史，戍金墉，為燕將慕容恪所陷，不屈見殺，贈東陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jin was long-time aide to Champion General Chen You, garrisoned Jinyong, was taken by Yan general Murong Ke, refused submission and was killed, and was posthumously made Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jin served as long-time aide to Champion General Chen You, garrisoned Jinyong, was captured by Yan general Murong Ke, refused submission and was killed, and was posthumously made Administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 祖赤黔，廷尉卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chiqian was Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chiqian served as Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 父叔任，少有幹質，朱齡石伐蜀，為齡石建威府司馬。

translations.literal: His father Shuren had capacity and substance in youth; when Zhu Lingshi campaigned against Shu he was acting marshal on Lingshi's Army That Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuren showed capacity and substance in youth; when Zhu Lingshi campaigned against Shu he served as acting marshal on Lingshi's Army That Establishes Might staff.

sentences.zh: 平蜀之功，亞于元帥，以功封寧新縣男。

translations.literal: In the pacification of Shu his merit was second only to the commander-in-chief, and for merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Ningxin County.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shu campaign his merit ranked second only to the commander-in-chief, and he was enfeoffed Baron of Ningxin County.

sentences.zh: 後拜益州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Inspector of Yi Province and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Inspector of Yi Province and died in office.

sentences.zh: 演之年十一，尚書僕射劉柳見而知之，曰：「此童終為令器。

translations.literal: When Yanzhi was eleven, Vice Director of the Secretariat Liu Liu saw and recognized him, saying, "This child will in the end be a fine vessel."
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhi was eleven, Vice Director Liu Liu saw him and declared, "This boy will become a fine vessel."

sentences.zh: 」沈氏家世為將，而演之折節好學，讀老子百遍，以義理業尚知名。

translations.literal: The Shen family for generations had been military men, yet Yanzhi restrained himself and loved learning; he read the Laozi a hundred times and was known for upholding principle.
translations.idiomatic: The Shen clan had been soldiers for generations, yet Yanzhi restrained himself and loved learning; he read the Laozi a hundred times and won renown for moral principle.

sentences.zh: 襲父別爵吉陽縣五等侯。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's separate enfeoffment as Marquis of Jiyang County, fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's separate enfeoffment as fifth-rank Marquis of Jiyang County.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，為嘉興令，有能名。

translations.literal: Recommended as Outstanding Talent, he became Magistrate of Jiaxing and gained a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Outstanding Talent, he became Magistrate of Jiaxing and earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，累遷尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era he was promoted step by step to Director of Personnel in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanjia era he rose step by step to Director of Personnel in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 先是劉湛、劉斌等結黨，欲排廢尚書僕射殷景仁。

translations.literal: Earlier Liu Zhan, Liu Bin, and others had formed a faction intending to drive out Vice Director Yin Jingren.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Zhan, Liu Bin, and others had formed a faction aiming to drive out Vice Director Yin Jingren.

sentences.zh: 演之雅仗正義，與景仁素善，盡心朝廷。

translations.literal: Yanzhi always relied on righteousness, was on good terms with Jingren, and gave his full loyalty to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi always stood on righteousness, was close to Jingren, and gave the court his full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 文帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 及彭城王義康出蕃，誅劉湛等，以演之為右衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Prince of Pengcheng Yikang went out to his fief and Liu Zhan and others were executed, Yanzhi was made General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Pengcheng Yikang went to his fief and Liu Zhan and others were executed, Yanzhi became General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 景仁尋卒，乃以後軍長史范曄為左衛將軍，與演之對掌禁旅，同參機密。

translations.literal: When Jingren soon died, Rear Army Chief Aide Fan Ye was made General of the Left Guard and, with Yanzhi, jointly commanded the palace guard and shared confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingren soon died, Rear Army Chief Aide Fan Ye became General of the Left Guard; he and Yanzhi jointly commanded the palace guard and shared confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋加侍中，文帝謂之曰：「侍中領衛，望實優顯，此蓋宰相便坐，卿其勉之。」

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional title of Palace Attendant; Emperor Wen said to him, "Palace Attendant commanding the guard—honor and substance both excel; this is virtually the premier's seat beside the throne. You must exert yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received the additional title Palace Attendant; Emperor Wen told him, "Palace Attendant commanding the guard—honor and substance both excel; this is virtually the premier's seat beside the throne. Apply yourself."

sentences.zh: 上欲伐林邑，朝臣多不同；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to attack Lin-yi; most court officials disagreed;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to attack Lin-yi; most court officials opposed the plan;

sentences.zh: 唯廣州刺史陸徽與演之贊成上意。

translations.literal: only Inspector of Guang Province Lu Hui and Yanzhi supported the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: only Inspector of Guang Province Lu Hui and Yanzhi supported it.

sentences.zh: 及林邑平，賜群臣黃金生口銅器等物，演之所得偏多。

translations.literal: When Lin-yi was pacified the emperor bestowed on the officials gold, captives, bronze vessels, and other goods; Yanzhi received a larger share.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin-yi fell the emperor bestowed gold, captives, bronze vessels, and other goods on the officials; Yanzhi received an unusually large share.

sentences.zh: 上謂曰：「廟堂之謀，卿參其力，平此遠夷，未足多建茅土。

translations.literal: The emperor said to him, "In the court's planning you shared the effort; to pacify this distant barbarian land is not enough to raise you to a great fief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "You shared in the court's planning; pacifying this distant land is not enough to raise you to a great fief.

sentences.zh: 俟廓清舊都，鳴鸞東岱，不憂河山之不開也。」

translations.literal: Wait until the old capital is cleared and the imperial carriage sounds at Mount Tai—then do not worry that mountains and rivers will not open."
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the old capital is cleared and the imperial carriage sounds at Mount Tai—then the realm's mountains and rivers will open to you."

sentences.zh: 二十一年，詔以演之為中領軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year an edict made Yanzhi General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-one an edict appointed Yanzhi General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 太子詹事范曄懷逆謀，演之覺其有異，言之文帝，曄尋伏誅。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Tutor Fan Ye harbored treasonous designs; Yanzhi perceived his strangeness, reported it to Emperor Wen, and Ye was soon executed.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Tutor Fan Ye harbored treason; Yanzhi detected his strangeness, reported it to Emperor Wen, and Ye was soon executed.

sentences.zh: 歷位吏部尚書，領太子右衛率。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Minister of Personnel and concurrent Commander of the Crown Prince's Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of Personnel and concurrent Commander of the Crown Prince's Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 素有心氣，寢病歷年。

translations.literal: He had long suffered from heart qi and lay ill for years.
translations.idiomatic: He had long suffered heart qi disorder and lay ill for years.

sentences.zh: 上使臥疾理事。

translations.literal: The emperor had him conduct affairs while bedridden.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him conduct business from his sickbed.

sentences.zh: 性好舉才，申濟屈滯，而謙約自持，上賜女伎，不受。

translations.literal: By nature he loved promoting talent and relieving the blocked and stagnant, yet he kept himself modest and restrained; the emperor bestowed female performers and he would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved promoting talent and relieving the blocked and stagnant, yet remained modest; the emperor bestowed female performers and he refused them.

sentences.zh: 暴卒。

translations.literal: He died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: He died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 文帝痛惜，贈金紫光祿大夫，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen grieved deeply and posthumously made him Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, with the posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen grieved deeply and posthumously made him Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle with the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子睦，位黃門侍郎，與弟西陽王文學勃忿鬩，坐徙始興郡。

translations.literal: His son Mu reached the post of Gentleman at the Yellow Gate; he quarreled with his younger brother, Literary Scholar Bo of Xiyang, and was banished to Shixing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mu rose to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate; quarreling with his younger brother Bo, Literary Scholar to Prince of Xiyang, he was banished to Shixing Commandery.

sentences.zh: 勃輕薄好利，位太子右衛率，加給事中，坐贓賄徙梁州。

translations.literal: Bo was frivolous and greedy; he reached Commander of the Crown Prince's Right Guard with the additional title of Chief Drafting Officer, and was banished to Liang Province for bribery.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was frivolous and greedy; he rose to Commander of the Crown Prince's Right Guard with the additional title Chief Drafting Officer, then was banished to Liang Province for bribery.

sentences.zh: 後還，結事阮佃夫、王道隆等，位司徒左長史，為後廢帝所誅。

translations.literal: Later he returned, attached himself to Ruan Tianfu and Wang Daolong, reached Senior Aide of the Left in the Secretariat, and was executed by the deposed emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned, attached himself to Ruan Tianfu and Wang Daolong, rose to Senior Aide of the Left in the Secretariat, and was executed by the deposed emperor.

sentences.zh: 演之兄子坦之，仕齊位都官郎。

translations.literal: Yanzhi's elder brother's son Tanzhi served Qi and reached Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi's nephew Tanzhi served Qi and rose to Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 坦之子顗。

translations.literal: Tanzhi's son Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi's son was Yi.

sentences.zh: 顗字處默，幼清靜有至行，慕黃叔度、徐孺子之為人，讀書不為章句，著述不尚浮華。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Chumo, from youth was quiet and of utmost conduct; he admired Huang Shudu and Xu Ruzi, read without parsing clauses, and in writing did not pursue ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, courtesy name Chumo, was quiet from youth and of utmost integrity; he admired Huang Shudu and Xu Ruzi, read without parsing clauses, and wrote without chasing ornament.

sentences.zh: 常獨處一室，人罕見其面。

translations.literal: He often stayed alone in one room and people rarely saw his face.
translations.idiomatic: He often kept to a single room alone, and few ever saw his face.

sentences.zh: 從叔勃貴顯，每還吳興，賓客填咽，顗不至其門。

translations.literal: When his uncle Bo became eminent and returned to Wu Commandery, guests filled the courtyard, yet Yi never came to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: When his uncle Bo rose high and returned to Wu Commandery, guests choked the courtyard, yet Yi never appeared at his gate.

sentences.zh: 勃就之，顗送迎不越閫。

translations.literal: Bo went to him; Yi received and sent him off without crossing the threshold.
translations.idiomatic: Bo went to visit him; Yi received and saw him off without crossing the threshold.

sentences.zh: 勃歎曰：「吾乃今知貴不如賤也。」

translations.literal: Bo sighed and said, "Only now do I know that eminence is not as good as obscurity."
translations.idiomatic: Bo sighed and said, "Only now do I see that eminence is not as good as obscurity."

sentences.zh: 顗內行甚修，事母兄孝友。

translations.literal: Yi's inner conduct was greatly cultivated; he served his mother and elder brother with filial piety and brotherly love.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's private conduct was deeply cultivated; he served mother and elder brother with filial piety and brotherly devotion.

sentences.zh: 兄昂一名顒，亦退素，以家貧仕為始安令。

translations.literal: His elder brother Ang, also called Yong, was likewise retiring and plain; because the family was poor he took office as Magistrate of Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Ang, also called Yong, was likewise retiring; poor as the family was, he took office as Magistrate of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 兄弟不能分離，相隨之任。

translations.literal: The brothers could not part and followed each other to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers could not bear separation and followed each other to the post.

sentences.zh: 梁天監四年，大舉北侵，南陽樂藏為武康令，以顗從役到建鄴，揚州別駕陸任以書與吳興太守柳惲，責之不能甄善別賢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjian, when a great northern campaign was launched, Yue Zang of Nanyang was Magistrate of Wukang; Yi was conscripted and reached Jiankang; Assistant Prefect of Yang Province Lu Ren wrote to Administrator of Wu Commandery Liu Yun blaming him for failing to distinguish worth from unworth.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianjian, during a great northern campaign, Yue Zang of Nanyang was Magistrate of Wukang; Yi was conscripted and reached Jiankang; Yang Province Assistant Prefect Lu Ren wrote Administrator Liu Yun blaming him for failing to distinguish worth from unworth.

sentences.zh: 惲大慚，即表停之。

translations.literal: Yun was greatly ashamed and immediately memorialized to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was deeply ashamed and immediately memorialized to halt the conscription.

sentences.zh: 卒家，所著文章數十篇。

translations.literal: He died at home and left several tens of written pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home, leaving several dozen written pieces.

sentences.zh: 憲字彥璋，演之從祖弟子也。

translations.literal: Xian, styled Yanzhang, was a younger clansman of Yanzhi's grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, courtesy name Yanzhang, was a younger clansman of Yanzhi's grandfather.

sentences.zh: 祖說道，巴西、梓潼二郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shuodao was Administrator of Baxi and Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shuodao had been Administrator of Baxi and Zitong.

sentences.zh: 父璞之，北中郎行參軍。

translations.literal: His father Puzhi was Acting Adjutant to the General of the North.
translations.idiomatic: His father Puzhi served as Acting Adjutant to the General of the North.

sentences.zh: 憲少有幹局，為駕部郎。

translations.literal: Xian had capacity and judgment in youth and became Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Xian showed capacity and judgment in youth and became Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝與憲棋，謂曰：「卿廣州刺史材也。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song played weiqi with Xian and said to him, "You have the stuff of a Guang Province inspector."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Song played weiqi with Xian and told him, "You have the makings of a Guang Province inspector."

sentences.zh: 」補烏程令，甚著政績，太守褚彥回歎美，以為方圓可施。

translations.literal: He was appointed Magistrate of Wucheng, achieved notable governance, and Administrator Chu Yanhui praised him as fit for both square rule and round flexibility.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Magistrate of Wucheng, he achieved notable governance; Administrator Chu Yanhui praised him as fit for both strict rule and flexible judgment.

sentences.zh: 少府管掌煩冗，材幹者並更其職，憲以吏能，累遷少府卿。

translations.literal: The Palace Storehouse managed many tangled duties; men of talent were rotated through its posts, and Xian by clerical ability was promoted step by step to Director of the Palace Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Storehouse managed tangled duties; capable men rotated through its posts, and Xian rose by clerical ability to Director of the Palace Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 武陵王曄為會稽，以憲為左軍司馬。

translations.literal: Prince of Wuling Ye was in Kuaiji and made Xian acting marshal of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wuling Ye held Kuaiji and made Xian acting marshal of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝以山陰戶眾，欲分為兩縣。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi, because Shanyin had a large population, wished to divide it into two counties.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Qi, because Shanyin had a large population, wished to split it into two counties.

sentences.zh: 武帝啟曰：「縣豈不可禦，但用不得人耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu memorialized, saying, "A county can certainly be governed—it is only that the wrong man is used."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu memorialized: "A county can certainly be governed—it is only that the wrong man is used."

sentences.zh: 」乃以憲帶山陰令，政聲大著。

translations.literal: He then had Xian concurrently serve as Magistrate of Shanyin, and his reputation for governance grew greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Xian concurrently serve as Magistrate of Shanyin, and Xian's reputation for governance soared.

sentences.zh: 孔珪請假東歸，謂人曰：「沈令料事特有天才。」

translations.literal: Kong Gui asked leave to return east and told people, "Magistrate Shen has a special genius for handling affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Gui asked leave to return east and remarked to others, "Magistrate Shen has a rare genius for affairs."

sentences.zh: 後為晉安王后軍長史、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: Later he became Chief Aide to Prince of Jin'an's Rear Army and Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Chief Aide to Prince of Jin'an's Rear Army and as Administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 西陽王子明代為南兗州，憲仍留為冠軍長史，太守如故。

translations.literal: When Prince of Xiyang Ziming replaced him in Southern Yan Province, Xian remained as Chief Aide to the Champion and kept his post as Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Xiyang Ziming replaced him in Southern Yan Province, Xian remained Chief Aide to the Champion and kept his post as Administrator.

sentences.zh: 永明八年，子明典簽劉道濟贓私百萬，為有司所奏，賜死。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming, Ziming's registrar Liu Daoji embezzled a million cash and was reported by the relevant offices and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongming, Ziming's registrar Liu Daoji embezzled a million cash; the relevant offices reported him and he was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 憲坐不糾，免官。

translations.literal: Xian was dismissed for failing to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Xian lost his post for failing to investigate.

sentences.zh: 後除散騎常侍，未拜，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Regular Attendant but died before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was named Regular Attendant but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 當時稱為良吏。

translations.literal: People of the time called him a good official.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries called him a good official.

sentences.zh: 憲同郡丘仲起先是為晉平郡，清廉自立。

translations.literal: Qiu Zhongqi of Xian's commandery had earlier been Administrator of Jinping and stood upright in integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Zhongqi of Xian's commandery had earlier served as Administrator of Jinping and stood upright in integrity.

sentences.zh: 褚彥回歎曰：「目見可欲，心能不亂，此楊公所以遺子孫也。

translations.literal: Chu Yanhui sighed and said, "To see what is desirable yet keep the heart unconfused—this is why Yang Gong left such to his descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yanhui sighed and said, "To see what is desirable yet keep the heart unconfused—this is why Yang Gong left such an example to his descendants."

sentences.zh: 」仲起字子震，位至廷尉，卒。

translations.literal: Zhongqi, styled Zizhen, reached Director of the Court of Justice and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqi, courtesy name Zizhen, rose to Director of the Court of Justice and died.

sentences.zh: 憲孫浚字叔源，少涉學有才幹，仕梁曆山陰、吳、建康三縣，並有能名。

translations.literal: Xian's grandson Jun, styled Shuyuan, from youth studied broadly and had talent; serving Liang he held Shanyin, Wu, and Jiankang counties in succession and won reputations for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's grandson Jun, courtesy name Shuyuan, studied broadly from youth and had talent; serving Liang he held Shanyin, Wu, and Jiankang counties in succession and won reputations for ability.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，累遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he was promoted step by step to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiqing he rose step by step to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時台城為侯景所圍，外援並至，景表請和，求解圍還江北。

translations.literal: At that time Terrace City was besieged by Hou Jing; outside relief forces all arrived; Jing submitted a petition seeking peace and asking to lift the siege and return north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Terrace City was besieged by Hou Jing; outside relief arrived; Jing petitioned for peace, asking to lift the siege and return north of the river.

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: An edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted the request.

sentences.zh: 遣右衛將軍柳津對景盟歃。

translations.literal: General of the Right Guard Liu Jin was sent to swear the oath with Jing.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Right Guard Liu Jin was dispatched to exchange oaths with Jing.

sentences.zh: 景知城內疾疫，稍無守備，因緩去期。

translations.literal: Jing knew pestilence raged inside the city and defenses were slackening, and so he slowly extended the deadline for withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Jing knew pestilence raged inside the city and defenses were slackening, and slowly extended the deadline for withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 城內知其背盟，復舉烽鼓噪。

translations.literal: Inside the city, learning he had broken the oath, again raised beacon fires and clamor.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city, learning he had broken the oath, they again raised beacon fires and clamor.

sentences.zh: 後數日，景復進表請和，簡文使浚往景所。

translations.literal: Several days later Jing again submitted a petition seeking peace, and Emperor Jianwen sent Jun to Jing's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Jing again petitioned for peace, and Emperor Jianwen sent Jun to Jing's camp.

sentences.zh: 景曰：「即日向熱，非復行時，政欲立效求停，君可見為申聞。

translations.literal: Jing said, "These days are turning hot and are no longer the season for marching; I only wish to establish merit and seek a halt—you may report this for me."
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "The days are turning hot—not a season for marching; I only wish to establish merit and seek a halt. Report this for me."

sentences.zh: 」浚曰：「大將軍此意，意在得城。

translations.literal: Jun said, "The Grand General's intent is to take the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jun replied, "The Grand General's intent is to take the city.

sentences.zh: 下風所聞，久已乏食，城內雖困，尚有兵糧。

translations.literal: What I have heard downwind is that food has long been exhausted; though the city is hard pressed, it still has troops and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Word below says your food is long exhausted; though the city is hard pressed, it still holds troops and grain.

sentences.zh: 朝廷恐和好乖貳，已密敕外軍：若台城傾覆，勿以二宮為念，當以死雪恥。

translations.literal: The court, fearing the peace will fail, has secretly ordered outside armies: if Terrace City falls, do not regard the two palaces—die to wipe away shame.
translations.idiomatic: The court, fearing treachery in the peace, has secretly ordered outside armies: if Terrace City falls, do not regard the two palaces—die to wipe away shame.

sentences.zh: 若不能決戰，當深壁自守。

translations.literal: If you cannot fight to the decision, deepen the walls and hold firm."
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot fight to a decision, then deepen your walls and hold firm."

sentences.zh: 大將軍十萬之眾，將欲何資？

translations.literal: With a hundred thousand troops, on what will the Grand General rely?"
translations.idiomatic: With a hundred thousand men, on what will the Grand General rely?"

sentences.zh: 」景橫刀於膝，瞋目叱之。

translations.literal: Jing laid a sword across his knees and glared and shouted at him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing set a sword across his knees and glared and shouted at him."

sentences.zh: 浚乃正色責景曰：「河南王人臣，而舉兵向闕。

translations.literal: Jun then sternly rebuked Jing, saying, "Prince of Henan is a subject who raised troops against the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jun then sternly rebuked Jing: "Prince of Henan is a subject who raised troops against the capital.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷已赦王罪結盟，口血未乾，而復翻背。

translations.literal: Now the court has pardoned your crime and sworn alliance; the oath blood is not yet dry, yet you turn and betray it.
translations.idiomatic: The court has pardoned your crime and sworn alliance; the oath blood is not yet dry, yet you turn and betray it.

sentences.zh: 沈浚六十之年，且天子使也，奉命而行，何用見脅。

translations.literal: Shen Jun is sixty years old and an envoy of the Son of Heaven; I carry orders and go—what use is intimidation?"
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jun is sixty and an envoy of the Son of Heaven; I carry orders and go—what use is intimidation?"

sentences.zh: 」徑去不顧。

translations.literal: He went straight away without looking back.
translations.idiomatic: He turned and left without a backward glance."

sentences.zh: 景歎曰：「是真司直也。

translations.literal: Jing sighed and said, "This is a true upright censor."
translations.idiomatic: Jing sighed and said, "Here is a true upright censor."

sentences.zh: 」然密銜之。

translations.literal: Yet secretly he harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in secret he nursed a grudge."

sentences.zh: 又勸張嵊立義，後得殺之。

translations.literal: He also urged Zhang Song to raise righteousness, and later had Jun killed.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged Zhang Song to raise a righteous force, and later had Jun killed.

sentences.zh: 江夷字茂遠，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Yi, styled Maoyuan, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yi, courtesy name Maoyuan, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖霦，晉護軍將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lin was Jin General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lin had been Jin General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 父敳，驃騎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His father Xiao was Military Adviser to the Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiao served as Military Adviser to the Rapid Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 夷少自藻厲，為後進之美。

translations.literal: From youth Yi cultivated himself and was a model among the younger generation.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yi cultivated himself and stood as a model among the younger generation.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝板為鎮軍行參軍，豫討桓玄功，封南郡州陵縣五等侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song provisionally appointed him Acting Adjutant to the Pacifying Army; for merit in suppressing Huan Xuan he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhouling County in Nan Commandery, fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu provisionally appointed him Acting Adjutant to the Pacifying Army; for merit suppressing Huan Xuan he was enfeoffed fifth-rank Marquis of Zhouling County in Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 累遷大司馬，武帝命大司馬府、琅邪國事，一以委焉。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to Grand Marshal; Emperor Wu entrusted all affairs of the Grand Marshal's office and the Principality of Langye to him.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Grand Marshal; Emperor Wu entrusted all affairs of the Grand Marshal's office and the Principality of Langye to him.

sentences.zh: 武帝受命，歷位吏部尚書，吳郡太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the mandate he successively held the posts of Minister of Personnel and Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu received the mandate he served successively as Minister of Personnel and Administrator of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 營陽王于吳縣見害，夷臨哭盡禮。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yingyang was killed at Wu County, Yi went to mourn and performed the full rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yingyang was killed at Wu County, Yi went to mourn and performed every rite.

sentences.zh: 以兄疾去官，後為右僕射。

translations.literal: Because of his elder brother's illness he left office; later he became Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He left office because of his elder brother's illness; later he became Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 夷美風儀，善舉止，歷任以和簡著稱。

translations.literal: Yi had fine bearing and graceful conduct, and in successive posts was known for harmony and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had fine bearing and graceful conduct; in successive posts he was known for harmony and simplicity.

sentences.zh: 出為湘州刺史，加散騎常侍，未之職，卒。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Xiang Province with the additional title Regular Attendant, did not take up the post, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Inspector of Xiang Province with the additional title Regular Attendant but died before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 遺令薄斂，蔬奠務存儉約。

translations.literal: His final instructions called for a plain burial and vegetable offerings kept strictly frugal.
translations.idiomatic: His final instructions called for a plain burial and strictly frugal vegetable offerings.

sentences.zh: 子湛。

translations.literal: His son was Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhan.

sentences.zh: 湛字徽深，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: Zhan, styled Huishen, was known for filial piety in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan, courtesy name Huishen, was known for filial piety in mourning.

sentences.zh: 愛文義，善彈棋鼓琴，兼明算術。

translations.literal: He loved literature and righteousness, was skilled at playing chess and the zither, and was also versed in calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He loved literature and righteousness, excelled at chess and the zither, and was versed in calculation.

sentences.zh: 為彭城王義康司徒主簿、之盛，人競求自昵，唯湛自疏，固求外出，乃以為武陵內史。

translations.literal: When Prince of Pengcheng Yikang was at the height of his power, people competed to seek his favor; only Zhan kept his distance and firmly sought an outside post, and so was made Interior Administrator of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Pengcheng Yikang stood at the height of power, men competed to seek his favor; only Zhan kept his distance and firmly sought an outside post, and was made Interior Administrator of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 隨王誕為北中郎將、南徐州刺史，以湛為長史、南東海太守，委以政事。

translations.literal: When Prince of Sui Wang Dan became General of the North and Inspector of Southern Xu Province, he made Zhan Chief Aide and Administrator of Eastern Donghai and entrusted him with government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Sui Wang Dan became General of the North and Inspector of Southern Xu Province, he made Zhan Chief Aide and Administrator of Eastern Donghai and entrusted him with government.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十五年，徵為侍中，任以機密。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia he was summoned as Palace Attendant and entrusted with confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year twenty-five he was summoned as Palace Attendant and entrusted with confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 遷左衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 時改選學職，以太尉江夏王義恭領國子祭酒，湛領博士。

translations.literal: At that time academic posts were reformed; Grand Commandant Prince of Jiangxia Yigong was made concurrent Director of the Imperial University, and Zhan was made concurrent Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: At that time academic posts were reformed; Grand Commandant Prince of Jiangxia Yigong became concurrent Director of the Imperial University, and Zhan concurrent Erudite.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 家甚貧，不營財利，餉饋盈門，一無所受。

translations.literal: His household was very poor; he did not pursue wealth, and though gifts filled his gate he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: His household was very poor; he pursued no wealth, and though gifts filled his gate he accepted none.

sentences.zh: 無兼衣餘食，嘗為上所召，遇澣衣，稱疾經日，衣成然後起。

translations.literal: He had no spare clothes or food; once when summoned by the emperor he was washing clothes, pleaded illness for a whole day, and only rose when the clothes were finished.
translations.idiomatic: He had no spare clothes or food; once summoned by the emperor while washing clothes, he pleaded illness for a whole day and only rose when the clothes were finished.

sentences.zh: 牛餓，御人求草，湛良久曰：「可與飲。

translations.literal: The ox was hungry and the driver sought fodder; Zhan after a long while said, "It may drink."
translations.idiomatic: The ox was hungry and the driver sought fodder; after a long pause Zhan said, "It may drink."

sentences.zh: 」在選職頗有刻核之譏，而公平無私，不受請謁，論者以此稱焉。

translations.literal: In the selection office he drew some criticism for severity, yet he was fair and without private favor and would not accept petitions; commentators praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: In the selection office he drew some criticism for severity, yet he was fair, accepted no private petitions, and commentators praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 初，上大舉北侵，舉朝謂為不可，唯湛贊成之。

translations.literal: At first, when the emperor launched a great northern campaign, the whole court said it could not be done; only Zhan supported it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first launched a great northern campaign, the whole court said it could not be done; only Zhan supported it.

sentences.zh: 及魏太武至瓜步，以湛兼領軍，軍事處分，一以委焉。

translations.literal: When Wei Emperor Taiwu reached Guabu, Zhan was given concurrent command of the army, and all military disposition was entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Emperor Taiwu reached Guabu, Zhan was given concurrent command of the army and all military disposition was entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 魏遣使求昏，上召太子劭以下集議。

translations.literal: Wei sent envoys seeking marriage; the emperor summoned Crown Prince Shao and those below to assemble for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent envoys seeking marriage; the emperor summoned Crown Prince Shao and the court below to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 眾並謂宜許，湛謂許之無益。

translations.literal: All said agreement should be granted; Zhan said granting it would bring no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: All said agreement should be granted; Zhan said it would bring no benefit.

sentences.zh: 劭怒謂湛曰：「今三王在阨，詎宜苟執異議。

translations.literal: Shao angrily said to Zhan, "The three princes are in peril—how can you stubbornly hold a different view?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao angrily told Zhan, "The three princes are in peril—how can you stubbornly hold a different view?"

sentences.zh: 」聲色甚厲。

translations.literal: His voice and expression were very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: His voice and tone were fiercely harsh."

sentences.zh: 坐散俱出，劭使班劍及左右推排之，殆於傾倒。

translations.literal: When the assembly dispersed and all went out, Shao sent armed guards and attendants to push and shove him, nearly overturning him.
translations.idiomatic: When the assembly dispersed, Shao sent armed guards and attendants to push and shove him, nearly overturning him.

sentences.zh: 劭後宴集，未嘗命湛，上乃為劭長子偉之娉湛第三女，欲以和之。

translations.literal: Later at banquets Shao never ordered Zhan to attend; the emperor then arranged for Shao's eldest son Weizhi to marry Zhan's third daughter, wishing to reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: Later at banquets Shao never summoned Zhan; the emperor then arranged for Shao's eldest son Weizhi to marry Zhan's third daughter, hoping to reconcile them.

sentences.zh: 上將廢劭，使湛具詔草。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to depose Shao, he had Zhan draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to depose Shao, he had Zhan draft the edict text.

sentences.zh: 劭之入弑，湛直上省，聞叫乃匿傍小屋。

translations.literal: When Shao entered to assassinate, Zhan went straight to the Secretariat; hearing the outcry he hid in a small room nearby.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao entered to assassinate, Zhan went straight to the Secretariat; at the outcry he hid in a small room nearby.

sentences.zh: 劭遣求之，舍吏紿云：「不在此」。

translations.literal: Shao sent men to seek him; the office clerk deceived them, saying, "He is not here."
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent men to find him; the office clerk lied, "He is not here."

sentences.zh: 兵即殺舍吏，乃得見湛。

translations.literal: The soldiers immediately killed the office clerk, and only then saw Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers immediately killed the office clerk, and only then found Zhan.

sentences.zh: 湛據窗受害，意色不橈。

translations.literal: Zhan leaned on the window and received the blow; his expression did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan leaned on the window and received the blow; his expression never changed.

sentences.zh: 五子恁、恕、憼、愻、法壽皆見殺。

translations.literal: His five sons Ren, Shu, Cong, Xun, and Fashou were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: His five sons Ren, Shu, Cong, Xun, and Fashou were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 初，湛家數見怪異，未敗少日，所眠床忽有數斗血。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhan's house had repeatedly seen strange omens; not many days before the disaster the bed where he slept suddenly held several pecks of blood.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier strange omens had repeatedly appeared in Zhan's house; not many days before the disaster, several pecks of blood suddenly appeared on the bed where he slept.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，追贈左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，諡曰忠簡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne he was posthumously made Left Grand Master of the Golden Seal, Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle with the same ceremonial as the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous title Loyal and Simple Duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne he was posthumously made Left Grand Master of the Golden Seal, Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle with Three Excellencies ceremonial, posthumous title Loyal and Simple Duke.

sentences.zh: 恁位著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Ren reached the post of Assistant Editor in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Ren rose to Assistant Editor in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 恁子斅。

translations.literal: Ren's son Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Ren's son was Jiao.

sentences.zh: 斅字叔文，母宋文帝女淮陽長公主。

translations.literal: Jiao, styled Shuwen, was the son of Princess Huaiyang, daughter of Emperor Wen of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao, courtesy name Shuwen, was son of Princess Huaiyang, daughter of Emperor Wen of Song.

sentences.zh: 幼以戚屬召見，孝武謂謝莊曰：「此小兒方當為名器。

translations.literal: Called in as a young kinsman of the imperial house, Emperor Xiaowu said to Xie Zhuang, "This small child will surely become a famous vessel."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned young as an imperial kinsman, Emperor Xiaowu told Xie Zhuang, "This boy will become a famous vessel."

sentences.zh: 」少有美譽，尚孝武女臨汝公主，拜駙馬都尉，為丹陽丞。

translations.literal: He had a fine reputation from youth, married Emperor Xiaowu's daughter Princess Linru, was appointed Commandant Consort, and became Assistant Prefect of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He had a fine reputation from youth, married Emperor Xiaowu's daughter Princess Linru, became Commandant Consort, and served as Assistant Prefect of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 時袁粲為尹，見斅歎曰：「風流不墜，政在江郎。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Can was Prefect; seeing Jiao he sighed and said, "Elegance has not fallen—the credit belongs to Master Jiang."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can was then Prefect; seeing Jiao he sighed and said, "Elegance has not fallen—the credit belongs to Master Jiang."

sentences.zh: 」數與宴賞，留連日夜。

translations.literal: He often feasted and rewarded him, keeping him day and night.
translations.idiomatic: He often feasted and rewarded him, keeping him for days and nights on end."

sentences.zh: 遷中書郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 斅庶祖母王氏老疾，斅視膳嘗藥，七十餘日不解衣。

translations.literal: Jiao's step-grandmother Lady Wang was old and ill; Jiao attended her meals and tasted her medicine, for more than seventy days without removing his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's step-grandmother Lady Wang was old and ill; Jiao attended her meals and tasted her medicine for more than seventy days without removing his clothes.

sentences.zh: 及累居內官，每以侍養陳請，朝廷優其朝直。

translations.literal: When he repeatedly held inner posts he each time petitioned to serve her; the court eased his attendance at court.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he held an inner post he petitioned to stay and serve her; the court eased his attendance at court.

sentences.zh: 初，湛娶褚秀之女，大義不終。

translations.literal: At first Zhan married the daughter of Chu Xiu; the marriage ended without completion.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhan had married the daughter of Chu Xiu, but the marriage was never completed.

sentences.zh: 褚彥回為衛軍，重斅為人，先通意，引為長史。

translations.literal: Chu Yanhui was General Who Guards the Army and valued Jiao as a man; he first expressed his intent and made Jiao his Chief Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yanhui was General Who Guards the Army and valued Jiao; he first expressed his intent and made Jiao his Chief Aide.

sentences.zh: 隨府轉司空長史，領臨淮太守。

translations.literal: Following the headquarters he was transferred to Chief Aide of the Minister of Works and concurrent Administrator of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Following the headquarters he became Chief Aide of the Minister of Works and concurrent Administrator of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 轉齊高帝太尉從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant of Affairs under the Grand Commandant of Emperor Gao of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant of Affairs under Emperor Gao of Qi's Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 齊台建，為吏部郎。

translations.literal: When the Qi regime was established he became Director of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi regime was established he was made Director of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 高帝即位，斅以祖母久疾，啟求自解。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao took the throne Jiao, because his grandmother's illness was long, memorialized asking to resign.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao took the throne, Jiao—his grandmother's illness being long—memorialized asking to resign.

sentences.zh: 初，宋明帝敕斅出繼其叔愻為從祖淳後，於是僕射王儉啟：「禮無後小宗之文，近代緣情，皆由父祖之命，未有既孤之後，出繼宗族也。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Ming of Song had ordered Jiao to succeed his uncle Xun as heir to his distant clansman Chun; then Vice Director Wang Jian memorialized, "Rites provide no text for adopting an heir in a lesser lineage; in recent times, moved by affection, all follow a father or grandfather's command—there is no precedent for leaving one's own lineage after becoming orphaned and then entering another clan.
