translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Ming of Song had ordered Jiao to succeed his uncle Xun as heir to distant clansman Chun; then Vice Director Wang Jian memorialized: "Rites provide no text for adopting an heir in a lesser lineage; in recent times, moved by affection, all follow a father or grandfather's command—there is no precedent for leaving one's own lineage after becoming orphaned and entering another clan.

sentences.zh: 雖復臣子一揆，而義非天屬。

translations.literal: Though minister and son are one measure, the bond is not of Heaven's kin.
translations.idiomatic: Though minister and son share one measure, the bond is not kin by Heaven.

sentences.zh: 江忠簡胤嗣所寄，唯斅一人，傍無期屬，斅宜還本。

translations.literal: The loyal and simple Jiang's line rests on Jiao alone; he has no close collateral kin—Jiao should return to his original house.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal and simple Jiang line rested on Jiao alone; with no close collateral kin, Jiao should return to his original house.

sentences.zh: 若不欲江愻絕後，可以斅小兒繼愻為孫。

translations.literal: If one does not wish Jiang Xun's line to end, Jiao's small son may succeed Xun as grandson."
translations.idiomatic: If one did not wish Jiang Xun's line to end, Jiao's young son might succeed Xun as grandson."

sentences.zh: 」尚書參議，謂「間世立後，禮無其文。

translations.literal: The Secretariat deliberated and said, "Establishing an heir across generations has no text in rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat deliberated: "Establishing an heir across generations has no text in rites.

sentences.zh: 荀顗無子立孫，墜禮之始。

translations.literal: Xun Yi, having no son, established a grandson—the beginning of falling from rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun Yi, having no son, established a grandson, it marked the beginning of falling from rite.

sentences.zh: 何琦又立此論，義無所據」。

translations.literal: He Qi again established this theory; in principle it has no basis."
translations.idiomatic: He Qi again advanced this theory; in principle it had no basis."

sentences.zh: 於是斅還本家，詔使自量立後者。

translations.literal: Jiao then returned to his original house; an edict had him choose an heir himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao then returned to his original house; an edict had him choose an heir for himself.

sentences.zh: 出為豫章內史，還除太子中庶子，未拜，門客通贓利，武帝遣信檢覆，斅藏此客而躬自引咎。

translations.literal: He went out as Interior Administrator of Yuzhang; on return he was appointed Crown Prince Household Supervisor but did not accept; a client trafficked in illicit profit, and Emperor Wu sent envoys to investigate—Jiao hid the client and took blame himself.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Interior Administrator of Yuzhang; on return he was appointed Crown Prince Household Supervisor but did not accept; a client trafficked in illicit profit, and Emperor Wu sent envoys to investigate—Jiao hid the client and took the blame himself.

sentences.zh: 上甚有怪色，王儉從容啟上曰：「江斅若能臨郡，此便是具美耳。

translations.literal: The emperor's expression was very displeased; Wang Jian calmly memorialized, "If Jiang Jiao can govern a commandery, this in itself is full merit."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked very displeased; Wang Jian calmly memorialized, "If Jiang Jiao can govern a commandery, that in itself is full merit."

sentences.zh: 」上意乃釋。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was then eased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger then subsided."

sentences.zh: 永明中，為竟陵王司馬。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era he became Marshal to Prince of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming he served as Marshal to Prince of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 斅好文辭，圍棋第五品，為朝貴中最。

translations.literal: Jiao loved literary composition; in weiqi he was fifth grade and stood highest among court nobles.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao loved literary composition; in weiqi he ranked fifth grade and stood highest among court nobles.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，曆五兵尚書，東海、吳二郡太守，復為侍中，轉都官尚書，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant, successively Minister of the Five Armies, Administrator of Donghai and Wu, again Palace Attendant, then Minister of Justice, and concurrent General of the Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He became Palace Attendant, successively Minister of the Five Armies, Administrator of Donghai and Wu, again Palace Attendant, then Minister of Justice, and concurrent General of the Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 王晏啟武帝曰：「江斅今重登禮閣，兼掌六軍，慈渥所覃，實有優忝；

translations.literal: Wang Yan memorialized Emperor Wu, saying, "Jiang Jiao now again ascends the Ritual Pavilion and concurrently commands the Six Armies; the favor shown him is indeed generous and excessive;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan memorialized Emperor Wu: "Jiang Jiao now again ascends the Ritual Pavilion and concurrently commands the Six Armies; the favor shown him is indeed generous and excessive;

sentences.zh: 但語其事任，殆同閑輩。

translations.literal: yet speaking of the substance of his duties, he is nearly the same as idle company.
translations.idiomatic: yet judged by the substance of his duties he was nearly the same as idle company.

sentences.zh: 天旨既欲升其名位，愚謂以侍中領驍騎，望實清顯，有殊納言。

translations.literal: Since Heaven's intent wishes to raise his name and rank, I foolishly think that Palace Attendant concurrently commanding the Valiant Cavalry—honor and substance both clear and eminent—is quite different from Drafting Officer."
translations.idiomatic: Since Heaven's intent wishes to raise his name and rank, I think Palace Attendant concurrently commanding the Valiant Cavalry—honor and substance both clear and eminent—is quite different from Drafting Officer."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「斅常啟吾，為其鼻中惡。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Jiao often told me it was because of the ailment in his nose.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Jiao often told me it was because of the ailment in his nose.

sentences.zh: 今既以何胤、王瑩還門下，故有此回換耳。」

translations.literal: Now that He Yin and Wang Ying have returned to the Gatehouse, this rotation was made for that reason alone."
translations.idiomatic: Now that He Yin; Wang Ying have returned to the Gatehouse, this rotation became made for that reason alone."

sentences.zh: 先是中書舍人紀僧真幸于武帝，稍曆軍校，容表有士風。

translations.literal: Earlier Palace Secretariat Attendant Ji Sengzhen was favored by Emperor Wu; he was gradually promoted through military posts and in bearing had the air of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Palace Secretariat Attendant Ji Sengzhen had enjoyed Emperor Wu's favor; he rose gradually through military posts and in bearing showed the air of a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 謂帝曰：「臣小人，出自本縣武吏，邀逢聖時，階榮至此。

translations.literal: He said to the emperor, "Your servant is a small man, born from a military clerk of his native county; meeting the sage age, step by step I reached this rank.
translations.idiomatic: He told the emperor, "I am a small man, born from a military clerk of my native county; meeting the sage age, step by step I reached this rank.

sentences.zh: 為兒昏，得荀昭光女，即時無復所須，唯就陛下乞作士大夫。

translations.literal: For my son's marriage I obtained the daughter of Xun Zhaoguang; now I need nothing further—only from Your Majesty I beg to become a gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: For my son's marriage I obtained the daughter of Xun Zhaoguang; now I want for nothing—only from Your Majesty I beg to be counted a gentleman."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「由江斅、謝淪，我不得措此意，可自詣之。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Because of Jiang Jiao and Xie Lun I could not arrange this intent—you may go to them yourself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Because of Jiang Jiao and Xie Lun I could not arrange this—you may go to them yourself."

sentences.zh: 」僧真承旨詣斅，登榻坐定，斅便命左右曰：「移吾床讓客。

translations.literal: Sengzhen accepted the order and went to Jiao; mounting the couch and sitting, Jiao at once ordered attendants, "Move my couch and yield the seat to the guest."
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen accepted the order and went to Jiao; once seated on the couch, Jiao at once ordered attendants, "Move my couch and yield the seat to the guest."

sentences.zh: 」僧真喪氣而退，告武帝曰：「士大夫故非天子所命。

translations.literal: Sengzhen lost spirit and withdrew, and told Emperor Wu, "Gentlemen are truly not what the Son of Heaven commands."
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen lost heart and withdrew, telling Emperor Wu, "Gentlemen are truly not what the Son of Heaven commands."

sentences.zh: 」時人重斅風格，不為權幸降意。

translations.literal: People of the time valued Jiao's bearing and would not lower themselves before the powerful and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries valued Jiao's bearing and would not lower themselves before the powerful and favored."

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，為侍中，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he became Palace Attendant and concurrent Director of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang year one he became Palace Attendant and concurrent Director of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 郁林廢，朝臣皆被召入宮。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yulin was deposed, court officials were all summoned into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yulin was deposed, every court official was summoned into the palace.

sentences.zh: 斅至雲龍門，方知廢立，托散動，醉吐車中而去。

translations.literal: Jiao reached Cloud Dragon Gate and only then learned of the deposition and replacement; he feigned loose bowels, got drunk, vomited in the carriage, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao reached Cloud Dragon Gate and only then learned of the deposition; he feigned loose bowels, got drunk, vomited in the carriage, and left.

sentences.zh: 蒨字彥標，幼聰警，讀書過口便誦。

translations.literal: Qian, styled Yanbiao, was clever and alert from youth; what he read he recited after one pass.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, courtesy name Yanbiao, was clever and alert from youth; what he read he recited after one pass.

sentences.zh: 選為國子生，舉高第，起家秘書郎，累遷廬陵王主簿。

translations.literal: Selected as a student of the Imperial University, recommended with high marks, he first entered office as Secretariat Gentleman and was promoted step by step to Chief Clerk to Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as Imperial University student and recommended with high marks, he first entered office as Secretariat Gentleman and rose step by step to Chief Clerk to Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 居父憂以孝聞，廬於墓側，明帝敕遣齋仗二十人防之墓所。

translations.literal: In mourning his father he was known for filial piety; he built a hut beside the tomb, and Emperor Ming sent twenty fasting guards to protect the tomb site.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning his father he was known for filial piety; he built a hut beside the tomb, and Emperor Ming sent twenty fasting guards to protect the tomb site.

sentences.zh: 服闋，累遷建安內史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was promoted step by step to Interior Administrator of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he rose step by step to Interior Administrator of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝起兵，遣甯朔將軍劉諓之為郡，蒨拒之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops he sent General Who Pacifies the North Liu Yanzhi to the commandery; Qian resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops he sent General Who Pacifies the North Liu Yanzhi to the commandery; Qian resisted.

sentences.zh: 及建鄴平，蒨坐禁錮，俄被原。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified Qian was imprisoned, but soon pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang was pacified Qian was imprisoned, but was soon pardoned.

sentences.zh: 曆太尉臨川王長史、尚書吏部郎，領右軍。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Chief Aide to the Grand Commandant Prince of Linchuan, Director of Personnel in the Secretariat, and concurrent Commander of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Chief Aide to Grand Commandant Prince of Linchuan, Director of Personnel in the Secretariat, and concurrent Commander of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 方雅有風格，僕射徐勉權重，唯蒨及王規與抗禮，不為之屈。

translations.literal: Square and elegant in bearing, Vice Director Xu Mian held great power, yet only Qian and Wang Gui matched him in ceremony and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Square and elegant in bearing, Vice Director Xu Mian held great power, yet only Qian and Wang Gui matched him in ceremony and would not bow.

sentences.zh: 勉因蒨門客翟景為子繇求昏於蒨女，不答。

translations.literal: Mian, because Qian's client Zhai Jing sought marriage for Mian's son Yao with Qian's daughter, received no answer.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qian's client Zhai Jing sought marriage for Mian's son Yao with Qian's daughter, Mian received no answer.

sentences.zh: 景再言之，乃杖景四十，由此與勉忤。

translations.literal: Jing spoke again; Qian then had Jing beaten forty strokes, and from this he was at odds with Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Jing spoke again; Qian then had Jing beaten forty strokes, and from this he fell out with Mian.

sentences.zh: 勉又為子求蒨弟葺及王泰女，二人並拒之。

translations.literal: Mian again sought marriage for his son with Qian's younger brother Qi and Wang Tai's daughter; both refused.
translations.idiomatic: Mian again sought marriage for his son with Qian's younger brother Qi and Wang Tai's daughter; both turned him down.

sentences.zh: 葺為吏部郎，坐杖曹中幹免官，泰以疾假出宅，乃遷散騎常侍，皆勉意也。

translations.literal: Qi was Director of Personnel and was dismissed for beating a bureau clerk; Tai took sick leave and left his residence, then was transferred to Regular Attendant—all at Mian's instigation.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was Director of Personnel and was dismissed for beating a bureau clerk; Tai took sick leave and left his residence, then was moved to Regular Attendant—all at Mian's instigation.

sentences.zh: 初，天監六年，詔以侍中常侍並侍帷幄，分門下二局入集書，其官品視侍中，而非華胄所悅，故勉斥泰為之。

translations.literal: At first, in the sixth year of Tianjian, an edict had Palace Attendants and Regular Attendants attend together beside the throne; the two Gatehouse bureaus entered the Compilation Office, their rank equal to Palace Attendant yet not pleasing to noble clans, so Mian pushed Tai into it.
translations.idiomatic: At first, in the sixth year of Tianjian, an edict had Palace Attendants and Regular Attendants attend together beside the throne; the two Gatehouse bureaus entered the Compilation Office, rank equal to Palace Attendant yet not pleasing to noble clans, so Mian pushed Tai into it.

sentences.zh: 蒨尋遷司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Qian was soon transferred to Senior Aide of the Left in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was soon moved to Senior Aide of the Left in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初王泰出閣，武帝謂勉云：「江蒨資歷，應居選部。

translations.literal: At first when Wang Tai left the inner palace, Emperor Wu told Mian, "Jiang Qian's qualifications should place him in the selection office."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Tai left the inner palace, Emperor Wu told Mian, "Jiang Qian's qualifications should place him in the selection office."

sentences.zh: 」勉曰：「蒨有眼患，又不悉人物。

translations.literal: Mian said, "Qian has an eye ailment and does not know people well."
translations.idiomatic: Mian replied, "Qian has an eye ailment and does not know people well."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: The matter then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter then stopped.

sentences.zh: 遷光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡肅。

translations.literal: When he died he was given the posthumous title Su.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he received the posthumous title Su.

sentences.zh: 蒨好學，尤悉朝儀故事，撰江左遺典三十卷，未就，卒。

translations.literal: Qian loved learning and especially knew court ritual and old precedents; he compiled thirty scrolls of Eastern Jin surviving institutions but did not finish before he died.
translations.idiomatic: Qian loved learning and especially knew court ritual and old precedents; he compiled thirty scrolls on Eastern Jin surviving institutions but died before finishing.

sentences.zh: 文集十五卷。

translations.literal: His collected writings were fifteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to fifteen scrolls.

sentences.zh: 蒨弟曇字彥德，少學涉有器度，位侍中太子詹事，承聖初卒。

translations.literal: Qian's younger brother Tan, styled Yande, from youth studied broadly and had capacity; he reached Palace Attendant and Crown Prince Tutor and died at the beginning of the Chengsheng era.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's younger brother Tan, courtesy name Yande, studied broadly from youth and had capacity; he rose to Palace Attendant and Crown Prince Tutor and died at the beginning of the Chengsheng era.

sentences.zh: 曇弟祿。

translations.literal: Tan's younger brother was Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's younger brother was Lu.

sentences.zh: 祿字彥遐，幼篤學有文章，工書善琴。

translations.literal: Lu, styled Yanxia, from youth studied deeply and had literary talent; he was skilled at calligraphy and the zither.
translations.idiomatic: Lu, courtesy name Yanxia, studied deeply from youth and had literary talent; he excelled at calligraphy and the zither.

sentences.zh: 形貌短小，神明俊發。

translations.literal: His form was short, yet his spirit was bright and outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Though short in stature, his spirit was bright and outstanding.

sentences.zh: 位太子洗馬、湘東王錄事參軍，以氣陵府王，王深憾焉。

translations.literal: He reached Crown Prince Reader and Recorder to Prince of Xiangdong; by temperament he overbore the prince, and the prince deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Crown Prince Reader and Recorder to Prince of Xiangdong; by temperament he overbore the prince, and the prince deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 廬陵威王續代為荊州，留為驃騎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Prince of Luling Wei Xu replaced him in Jing Province and retained him as Military Adviser to the Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Luling Wei Xu replaced him in Jing Province and kept him as Military Adviser to the Rapid Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 獻書告別，王答書乃致恨。

translations.literal: He submitted a letter of farewell; the prince's reply letter expressed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a letter of farewell; the prince's reply expressed resentment.

sentences.zh: 祿先為武寧郡，頗有資產，積錢於壁，壁為之倒，迮銅物皆鳴。

translations.literal: Lu had earlier been Administrator of Wuning and had considerable property; he piled coins against a wall until the wall collapsed and all the bronze vessels rang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu had earlier governed Wuning and amassed property; he piled coins against a wall until the wall collapsed and all the bronze vessels rang.

sentences.zh: 人戲之曰：「所謂'銅山西傾，洛鍾東應'者也。

translations.literal: People joked, "This is what they call 'the bronze mountain tilts west, the Luo bell answers east.'"
translations.idiomatic: People teased him, "This is what they call 'the bronze mountain tilts west, the Luo bell answers east.'"

sentences.zh: 」湘東王恨之既深，以其名祿，改字曰榮財，以志其忿。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangdong's resentment was already deep; because his name was Lu he changed his courtesy name to Rongcai to mark his anger.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiangdong's resentment ran deep; because his name was Lu he changed his courtesy name to Rongcai to mark his anger.

sentences.zh: 後為作唐侯相，卒。

translations.literal: Later he became Marquis of Zuotang in title and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he held the title Marquis of Zuotang and died.

sentences.zh: 撰列仙傳十卷行於世，及井絜皋木人賦、敗船詠，並以自喻。

translations.literal: He compiled ten scrolls of Biographies of Immortals circulating in the world, and essays on the Well, the Pure Stream, the Wooden Man, and the Ruined Boat—all as self-allegory.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled ten scrolls of Biographies of Immortals that circulated in the world, and essays on the Well, the Pure Stream, the Wooden Man, and the Ruined Boat—all as self-allegory.

sentences.zh: 子徽亦有文采，而清狂不慧，常以父為戲。

translations.literal: His son Hui also had literary talent but was pure and mad and unwise, often making his father the butt of jokes.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui also had literary talent but was pure, mad, and unwise, often making his father the butt of jokes.

sentences.zh: 蒨子紑。

translations.literal: Qian's son Gou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's son was Gou.

sentences.zh: 紑字含絜，幼有孝性，年十三，父蒨患眼，紑侍疾將期月，衣不解帶。

translations.literal: Gou, styled Hanjie, had filial nature from youth; at thirteen when his father Qian suffered eye disease, Gou attended the illness for nearly a month without removing his belt.
translations.idiomatic: Gou, courtesy name Hanjie, had filial nature from youth; at thirteen when his father Qian suffered eye disease, Gou attended the illness for nearly a month without removing his belt.

sentences.zh: 夜夢一僧云：「患眼者飲慧眼水必差。

translations.literal: At night he dreamed a monk said, "One with eye disease should drink Wisdom-Eye water and will be cured."
translations.idiomatic: At night he dreamed a monk said, "One with eye disease should drink Wisdom-Eye water and be cured."

sentences.zh: 」及覺說之，莫能解者。

translations.literal: When he woke and told it, no one could explain it.
translations.idiomatic: When he woke and told the dream, no one could explain it.

sentences.zh: 紑第三叔祿與草堂寺智者法師善，往訪之。

translations.literal: Gou's third uncle Lu was on good terms with the wise monk of Caotang Temple; he went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Gou's third uncle Lu was on good terms with the wise monk of Caotang Temple and went to visit him.

sentences.zh: 智者曰：「無量壽經雲，慧眼見真，能度彼岸。

translations.literal: The wise monk said, "The Infinite Life Sutra says, the Wisdom Eye sees truth and can cross to the far shore."
translations.idiomatic: The wise monk said, "The Infinite Life Sutra says the Wisdom Eye sees truth and can cross to the far shore."

sentences.zh: 」蒨乃因智者啟舍同夏縣界牛屯裏舍為寺，乞賜嘉名。

translations.literal: Qian then through the wise monk memorialized to donate his house in Niutun Village in Tongxia County as a temple and begged a fine name.
translations.idiomatic: Through the wise monk, Qian memorialized to donate his house in Niutun Village in Tongxia County as a temple and begged a fine name."

sentences.zh: 敕答云：「純臣孝子往往感應，晉時顏含遂見冥中送藥，又近見智者以卿第二息夢雲'飲慧眼水'。

translations.literal: The edict replied, "Pure ministers and filial sons often move heaven; in Jin times Yan Han received medicine sent from the unseen, and recently the wise monk, because your second son dreamed the words 'drink Wisdom-Eye water.'
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied, "Pure ministers and filial sons often move heaven; in Jin times Yan Han received medicine sent from the unseen, and recently the wise monk, because your second son dreamed the words 'drink Wisdom-Eye water,'

sentences.zh: 慧眼則五眼之一號，可以慧眼為名。

translations.literal: Wisdom Eye is the name of one of the Five Eyes—it may be named Wisdom Eye."
translations.idiomatic: Wisdom Eye is one of the Five Eyes—it may take that name."

sentences.zh: 」及就創造，泄故井，井水清洌，異於恒泉。

translations.literal: When construction began an old well was opened; the well water was clear and different from ordinary springs.
translations.idiomatic: When construction began an old well was opened; the water was clear and unlike ordinary springs.

sentences.zh: 依夢取水洗眼及煮藥，稍覺有瘳，因此遂差。

translations.literal: Following the dream they took the water to wash the eyes and brew medicine; he gradually felt improvement and was thereby cured.
translations.idiomatic: Following the dream they took the water to wash the eyes and brew medicine; he gradually improved and was thereby cured.

sentences.zh: 時人謂之孝感。

translations.literal: People of the time called it filial response moving heaven.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time called it filial piety moving heaven.

sentences.zh: 南康王為徐州，召為迎主簿。

translations.literal: Prince of Nankang was in Xu Province and summoned him as Chief Reception Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Nankang held Xu Province he summoned Gou as Chief Reception Clerk.

sentences.zh: 紑性沈靜，好莊、老玄言，尤善佛義，不樂進仕。

translations.literal: Gou's nature was quiet; he loved Zhuangzi, Laozi, and dark learning, and was especially versed in Buddhist doctrine; he did not love advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Gou was quiet by nature; he loved Zhuangzi, Laozi, and dark learning, was especially versed in Buddhist doctrine, and did not love advancement.

sentences.zh: 及父卒，紑廬於墓，終日號慟不絕聲，月餘乃卒。

translations.literal: When his father died Gou built a hut at the tomb and wailed all day without stopping his voice; after more than a month he died.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died Gou built a hut at the tomb and wailed all day without stopping; after more than a month he died.

sentences.zh: 子總。

translations.literal: His son was Zong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zong.

sentences.zh: 總字總持，七歲而孤，依於外氏。

translations.literal: Zong, styled Zongchi, was orphaned at seven and lived with his maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: Zong, courtesy name Zongchi, was orphaned at seven and lived with his maternal kin.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏，有至性。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and had utmost nature.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was clever and of utmost nature.

sentences.zh: 元舅吳平侯蕭勱名重當世，特所鍾愛，謂曰：「爾神采英拔，後之知名，當出吾右。」

translations.literal: His maternal uncle Marquis of Wuping Xiao Li was famous in the age and especially cherished him, saying, "Your spirit is outstanding; future renown will surpass mine."
translations.idiomatic: His maternal uncle Marquis of Wuping Xiao Li was famous in the age and especially cherished him, saying, "Your spirit is outstanding; your future renown will surpass mine."

sentences.zh: 及長，篤學有文辭。

translations.literal: When grown he studied deeply and had literary skill.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he studied deeply and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: Serving Liang he became Director of the Palace in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Liang he rose to Director of the Palace in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武帝撰正言始畢，制述懷詩，總預同此作。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu finished compiling the Correct Words and composed a poem expressing his feelings; Zong participated in this composition.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu finished compiling the Correct Words and composed a poem expressing his feelings, Zong took part in the composition.

sentences.zh: 帝覽總詩，深見嗟賞。

translations.literal: The emperor read Zong's poem and deeply admired it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read Zong's poem and admired it deeply.

sentences.zh: 轉侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射范陽張纘、度支尚書琅邪王筠、都官尚書南陽劉之遴並高才碩學，總時年少有名，纘等雅相推重，為忘年友會。

translations.literal: Vice Director Zhang Zuan of Fanyang, Minister of Revenue Wang Yun of Langye, and Minister of Justice Liu Zhilin of Nanyang were all men of high talent and deep learning; Zong was then young and famous, and they deeply respected him and became friends across generations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuan of Fanyang, Wang Yun of Langye, and Liu Zhilin of Nanyang were all men of high talent and deep learning; Zong was then young and famous, and they deeply respected him and became friends across generations.

sentences.zh: 之遴嘗酬總詩，深相欽挹。

translations.literal: Zhilin once responded to Zong's poem and deeply admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilin once responded to Zong's poem and admired him deeply.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子中舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to Crown Prince Household Aide.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Crown Prince Household Aide.

sentences.zh: 侯景寇建鄴，詔以總權兼太常卿，守小廟。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing raided Jiankang an edict made Zong acting Grand Minister of Ceremonies guarding the lesser temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing raided Jiankang an edict made Zong acting Grand Minister of Ceremonies to guard the lesser temple.

sentences.zh: 台城陷，避難會稽郡，憩於龍華寺，乃制修心賦。

translations.literal: When Terrace City fell he took refuge in Kuaiji Commandery and rested at Longhua Temple, where he composed an essay on cultivating the heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Terrace City fell he took refuge in Kuaiji Commandery, rested at Longhua Temple, and composed an essay on cultivating the heart.

sentences.zh: 總第九舅蕭勃先據廣州，又自會稽往依焉。

translations.literal: Zong's ninth maternal uncle Xiao Bo had earlier seized Guang Province; Zong again went from Kuaiji to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's ninth maternal uncle Xiao Bo had earlier seized Guang Province; Zong again went from Kuaiji to join him.

sentences.zh: 及元帝平侯景，徵為始興內史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan pacified Hou Jing he was summoned as Interior Administrator of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Yuan pacified Hou Jing he became summoned as Interior Administrator of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 會魏克江陵，不行，自此流寓嶺南積歲。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling he did not go; from then he wandered in Lingnan for years.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei captured Jiangling he did not go; from then he wandered in Lingnan for many years.

sentences.zh: 陳天嘉四年，以中書侍郎征還。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancheng of Chen he was summoned back as Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In Chen Tiancheng year four he was summoned back as Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 累遷左戶尚書，轉太子詹事。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to Minister of the Left Household and transferred to Crown Prince Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Minister of the Left Household and became Crown Prince Tutor.

sentences.zh: 總性寬和溫裕，尤工五言七言，溺於浮靡。

translations.literal: Zong's nature was broad, gentle, and generous; he was especially skilled in five- and seven-character verse and drowned in ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Zong was broad, gentle, and generous by nature; he was especially skilled in five- and seven-character verse and drowned in ornament.

sentences.zh: 及為宮端，與太子為長夜之飲，養良娣陳氏為女，太子亟微行遊總家，宣帝怒免之。

translations.literal: When he became tutor to the palace he drank through the night with the crown prince, raised Lady Chen the good concubine as a daughter, and the crown prince often slipped out to visit Zong's house; Emperor Xuan was angry and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: When he became palace tutor he drank through the night with the crown prince, raised Lady Chen the good concubine as a daughter, and the crown prince often slipped out to visit Zong's house; Emperor Xuan was angry and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 後又曆侍中、左戶尚書。

translations.literal: Later he again successively held Palace Attendant and Minister of the Left Household.
translations.idiomatic: Later he again held Palace Attendant and Minister of the Left Household in succession.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年，陳亡入隋，拜上開府。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming Chen fell and he entered Sui; he was appointed Senior General Opening Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year three Chen fell and he entered Sui; he was appointed Senior General Opening Offices.

sentences.zh: 開皇十四年，卒于江都，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kaihuang he died at Jiangdu, age seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year fourteen he died at Jiangdu, age seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 其為自序云：「太建之時，權移群小，諂嫉作威，屢被摧黜，奈何命也。

translations.literal: In his self-account he wrote, "In the Taijian era power shifted to petty men, flattery and jealousy made authority, and I was repeatedly cast down—such is fate."
translations.idiomatic: In his self-account he wrote, "During Taijian power shifted to petty men, flattery and jealousy made authority, and I was repeatedly cast down—such is fate."

sentences.zh: 」識者譏其言跡之乖。

translations.literal: Those who understood mocked the gap between his words and deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Those who saw clearly mocked the gap between his words and deeds."

sentences.zh: 有文集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had collected writings of thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings of thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 長子溢，頗有文辭，性傲誕驕物，雖近屬故友，不免詆欺。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yi had considerable literary skill but was proud, reckless, and insulting; even close kin and old friends were not spared slander.
translations.idiomatic: The subject's eldest son Yi had considerable literary skill but became proud, reckless,; insulting; even close kin; old friends were not spared slander.

sentences.zh: 曆中書黃門侍郎，太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He successively held Gentleman of the Secretariat and Yellow Gate and Crown Prince Household Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: He held in succession Gentleman of the Secretariat and Yellow Gate and Crown Prince Household Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 入隋，為秦王文學，卒。

translations.literal: Entering Sui he became Literary Scholar to Prince of Qin and died.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Sui he became Literary Scholar to Prince of Qin and died there.

sentences.zh: 江智深，夷之弟子也。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhishen was a nephew of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhishen was Yi's nephew.

sentences.zh: 父僧安，宋太子中庶子。

translations.literal: His father Seng'an was Crown Prince Household Supervisor under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His father Seng'an had been Crown Prince Household Supervisor under Song.

sentences.zh: 夷有盛名，夷子湛又有清譽，父子並貴達。

translations.literal: Yi had a great name; Yi's son Zhan also had a pure reputation; father and son were both eminent and successful.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had a great name, and Yi's son Zhan a pure reputation; father and son were both eminent and successful.

sentences.zh: 智深父少無名問，湛禮敬甚簡，智深常以為恨，自非節歲不入湛門。

translations.literal: Zhishen's father from youth had no name or reputation; Zhan's courtesy was very sparse, and Zhishen always resented this, entering Zhan's gate only on festival days.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishen's father had no name from youth; Zhan's courtesy was very sparse, and Zhishen always resented this, entering Zhan's gate only on festival days.

sentences.zh: 及為隨王誕後軍參軍，在襄陽，誕待之甚厚。

translations.literal: When he became Rear Army Aide to Prince of Sui Wang Dan in Xiangyang, Dan treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became Rear Army Aide to Prince of Sui Wang Dan in Xiangyang, Dan treated him very generously.

sentences.zh: 時諮議參軍謝莊、主簿沈懷文與智深友善，懷文每稱曰：「人所應有盡有、所應無盡無者，其江智深乎。」

translations.literal: At that time Military Adviser Xie Zhuang and Chief Clerk Shen Huaiwen were on good terms with Zhishen; Huaiwen often praised him, saying, "What a man ought to have he has entirely; what he ought not to have he entirely lacks—can this be anyone but Jiang Zhishen?"
translations.idiomatic: Military Adviser Xie Zhuang and Chief Clerk Shen Huaiwen were then on good terms with Zhishen; Huaiwen often praised him, saying, "What a man ought to have he has entirely; what he ought not to have he entirely lacks—can this be anyone but Jiang Zhishen?"

sentences.zh: 元嘉末，除尚書庫部郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia he was appointed Director of the Storehouse in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanjia he was made Director of the Storehouse in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時高流官序不為台郎，智深門孤援寡，獨有此選，意甚不悅，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: At that time men of high standing did not take Secretariat clerk posts; Zhishen's house was isolated and without support, and he alone received this selection; he was very displeased and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Men of high standing then did not take Secretariat clerk posts; Zhishen's house was isolated and without support, and he alone received this selection; he was very displeased and firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 後為竟陵王誕司空主簿、記室參軍，領南濮陽太守，遷從事中郎。

translations.literal: Later he became Chief Clerk and Recorder to Prince of Jingling Wang Dan, Minister of Works, concurrent Administrator of Southern Puyang, and was transferred to Attendant of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Chief Clerk and Recorder to Prince of Jingling Wang Dan, Minister of Works, concurrent Administrator of Southern Puyang, and was moved to Attendant of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 誕將為逆，智深悟其機，請假先反。

translations.literal: When Dan was about to rebel Zhishen perceived the signs and asked leave to return first.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan was about to rebel Zhishen saw the signs and asked leave to return first.

sentences.zh: 誕事發，即除中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Dan's affair broke out he was immediately appointed Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan's affair broke out he was immediately made Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 智深愛好文雅，辭采清贍，孝武深相知待，恩禮冠朝。

translations.literal: Zhishen loved elegance and literary grace; his diction was clear and rich; Emperor Xiaowu knew and treated him deeply, and favor and ceremony topped the court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishen loved elegance; his diction was clear and rich; Emperor Xiaowu knew and treated him deeply, and favor and ceremony topped the court.

sentences.zh: 上宴私甚數，多命群臣五三人游集，智深常為其首。

translations.literal: The emperor feasted privately very often, often ordering three or five ministers to gather; Zhishen was regularly first among them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held private feasts very often, usually summoning three or five ministers at a time; Zhishen was regularly placed first among them.

sentences.zh: 同侶未及前，輒獨蒙引進，每以越眾為慚，未嘗有喜色。

translations.literal: Before his companions arrived he alone would be summoned in advance; he always felt ashamed to surpass the crowd and never showed a pleased expression.
translations.idiomatic: Before his companions arrived he alone would be summoned in advance; he always felt ashamed to surpass the crowd and never showed pleasure.

sentences.zh: 每從遊幸，與群僚相隨，見傳詔馳來，知當呼己，聳動愧恧，形於容貌，論者以此多之。

translations.literal: Each time he followed tours with the group of officials; seeing a relay edict gallop up and knowing he would be called, he would start and flush with shame, showing it in his face; commentators for this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he followed tours with officials; seeing a relay edict gallop up and knowing he would be called, he would start and flush with shame; commentators praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 遷驍騎將軍、尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Valiant Cavalry and Director of Personnel in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to General of the Valiant Cavalry and Director of Personnel in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上每酣宴，輒詆群臣，並使自相嘲訐，以為歡笑。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor drank deeply at feasts he would revile the ministers and also have them mock one another for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor drank deeply at feasts he would revile the ministers and have them mock one another for amusement.

sentences.zh: 智深素方退，漸不會旨。

translations.literal: Zhishen was by nature square and retiring and gradually failed to match the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishen was by nature square and retiring and gradually failed to match the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 上嘗使以王僧朗戲其子景文，智深正色曰：「恐不宜有此戲。

translations.literal: Once the emperor had him jest with Wang Senglang about his son Jingwen; Zhishen sternly said, "I fear this jest is not fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor had him jest with Wang Senglang about his son Jingwen; Zhishen said sternly, "I fear this jest is not fitting."

sentences.zh: 」上怒曰：「江僧安癡人，癡人自相惜。

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said, "Jiang Seng'an is a fool, and fools cherish one another."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped, "Jiang Seng'an is a fool, and fools cherish one another."

sentences.zh: 」智深伏席流涕，由此恩寵大衰。

translations.literal: Zhishen prostrated himself on the mat and wept; from this favor greatly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishen prostrated himself on the mat and wept; from this favor greatly declined."

sentences.zh: 出為新安王子鸞北中郎長史、南東海太守，行南徐州事。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Aide to Prince of Xin'an Ziluan, General of the North, and Administrator of Eastern Donghai, acting in Southern Xu Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Chief Aide to Prince of Xin'an Ziluan, General of the North, and Administrator of Eastern Donghai, handling Southern Xu Province affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，上寵姬宣貴妃殷氏卒，使群臣議諡，智深上議曰：「懷」。

translations.literal: At first, when the emperor's beloved concubine Lady Yin of the Honored Consort died, he had the ministers deliberate her posthumous title; Zhishen submitted the title Huai.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's beloved concubine Lady Yin of the Honored Consort died, he had the ministers deliberate her posthumous title; Zhishen submitted the title Huai.

sentences.zh: 上以不盡嘉號，甚銜之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because it did not fully express praise, deeply harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Because the title did not fully express praise, the emperor deeply harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 後車駕幸南山，乘馬至殷氏墓，群臣皆騎從，上以馬鞭指墓石柱謂智深曰：「此柱上不容有'懷'字「，智深益惶懼，以憂卒。

translations.literal: Later when the imperial carriage visited South Mountain and rode to Lady Yin's tomb, the ministers all rode in attendance; the emperor pointed with his whip at the tomb pillar and said to Zhishen, "On this pillar there is no room for the character 'Huai,'" and Zhishen grew still more fearful and died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Later the imperial carriage visited South Mountain and rode to Lady Yin's tomb; the ministers all rode in attendance; the emperor pointed with his whip at the tomb pillar and told Zhishen, "On this pillar there is no room for the character 'Huai,'" and Zhishen grew still more fearful and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 子筠，太子洗馬，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Yun was Crown Prince Reader and died early.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yun was Crown Prince Reader and died young.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝皇后，筠之女也。

translations.literal: The deposed emperor's empress was Yun's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor's empress became Yun's daughter.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，以後父追贈金紫光祿大夫，筠妻王平望鄉君。

translations.literal: When the deposed emperor took the throne the empress's father was posthumously made Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, and Yun's wife Lady Wang was made Lady of Pingwang Township.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor took the throne the empress's father was posthumously made Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, and Yun's wife Lady Wang became Lady of Pingwang Township.

sentences.zh: 智深兄子概早孤，智深養之如子。

translations.literal: Zhishen's elder brother's son Gai was orphaned early; Zhishen raised him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishen's elder brother's son Gai was orphaned early; Zhishen raised him as his own son.

sentences.zh: 概曆黃門吏部郎，侍中，武陵王贊北中郎長史。

translations.literal: Gai successively held Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Director of Personnel, Palace Attendant, and Chief Aide to Prince of Wuling Zan, General of the North.
translations.idiomatic: Gai held in succession Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Director of Personnel, Palace Attendant, and Chief Aide to Prince of Wuling Zan, General of the North.

sentences.zh: 江秉之字玄叔，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Bingzhi, styled Xuanshu, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bingzhi, courtesy name Xuanshu, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖逌，晉太常。

translations.literal: His grandfather You was Jin Grand Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather You had been Jin Grand Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 父纂，給事中。

translations.literal: His father Zuan was Chief Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zuan served as Chief Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 秉之少孤，弟妹七人並幼，撫育姻娶，盡其心力。

translations.literal: Bingzhi was orphaned young; seven younger siblings and sisters were all small, and he reared them, arranged marriages, and gave his full heart and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi was orphaned young; seven younger siblings were all small, and he reared them, arranged marriages, and gave his full heart and strength.

sentences.zh: 宋少帝時，為永世、烏程令，以善政著名東土。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Shao of Song he was Magistrate of Yongshi and Wucheng and was famous in the east for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shao of Song he was Magistrate of Yongshi and Wucheng and won fame in the east for good governance.

sentences.zh: 徵為建康令，為政嚴察，部下肅然。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Magistrate of Jiankang; his governance was strict and searching, and subordinates were awed.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Magistrate of Jiankang; his governance was strict and searching, and subordinates stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 後為山陰令，人戶三萬，政事繁擾，訟訴殷積，階庭常數百人。

translations.literal: Later he was Magistrate of Shanyin; the household count was thirty thousand, government affairs were tangled and pressing, and lawsuits piled up with several hundred people constantly in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Magistrate of Shanyin; the household count was thirty thousand, government affairs were tangled and pressing, and several hundred litigants constantly filled the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 秉之禦繁以簡，常得無事。

translations.literal: Bingzhi met complexity with simplicity and often had no business.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi met complexity with simplicity and often had no backlog.

sentences.zh: 宋世唯顧覬之亦以省務著績，其餘雖復刑政修理，而未能簡事。

translations.literal: In the Song only Gu Jizhi was also known for reducing affairs; the rest though they regulated punishment and government could not simplify affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Song only Gu Jizhi was also known for reducing affairs; the rest though they regulated punishment and government could not simplify affairs.

sentences.zh: 以在縣有能，出補新安太守。

translations.literal: Because of ability in the county he went out as acting Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Recognized for ability in the county, he was posted out as acting Administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十二年，轉在臨海，並以簡約見稱，卒於官所。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to Linhai and in both was praised for simplicity; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year twelve he was transferred to Linhai and in both posts was praised for simplicity; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 得秩悉散之親故，妻子常饑寒。

translations.literal: He gave all his salary to kin and friends; wife and children were often cold and hungry.
translations.idiomatic: He gave all his salary to kin and friends; wife and children often went cold and hungry.

sentences.zh: 人有勸其營田，秉之正色答曰：「食祿之家，豈可與農人競利。

translations.literal: People urged him to farm fields; Bingzhi sternly replied, "Families living on salary—how can they compete for profit with farmers?"
translations.idiomatic: People urged him to farm; Bingzhi sternly replied, "Families living on salary—how can they compete for profit with farmers?"

sentences.zh: 」在郡作書案一枚，去官留以付庫。

translations.literal: In the commandery he made one writing desk; on leaving office he left it in the storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he made one writing desk; on leaving office he left it in the storehouse."

sentences.zh: 秉之宗人邃之字玄遠，頗有文義，撰文釋傳於世，位司徒記室參軍。

translations.literal: Bingzhi's clansman Suizhi, styled Xuanyuan, had considerable literary principle, compiled writings explaining the classics circulating in the world, and reached Recorder to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi's clansman Suizhi, courtesy name Xuanyuan, had considerable literary principle, compiled writings explaining the classics circulating in the world, and reached Recorder to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 秉之子徽，尚書都官郎，吳令。

translations.literal: Bingzhi's son Hui was Director of the Ministry of Justice in the Secretariat and Magistrate of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi's son Hui served as Director of the Ministry of Justice in the Secretariat and as Magistrate of Wu.

sentences.zh: 元凶殺徐湛之，徽以黨與見誅。

translations.literal: When the assassin prince killed Xu Zhanzhi, Hui was executed as an associate.
translations.idiomatic: When the assassin prince killed Xu Zhanzhi, Hui was executed as his associate.

sentences.zh: 子謐。

translations.literal: His son was Mi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Mi.

sentences.zh: 謐再遷右丞，兼比部朗。

translations.literal: Mi was twice transferred to Right Assistant Director and concurrently Director of the Comparison Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was twice moved to Right Assistant Director and concurrently Director of the Comparison Bureau.

sentences.zh: 泰始四年，江夏王義恭第十五女卒，年十九，未笄，禮官議從成人服，諸王服大功。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi, the fifteenth daughter of Prince of Jiangxia Yigong died at nineteen, unmarried; the ritual officers deliberated adult mourning, and the princes wore great mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi year four, the fifteenth daughter of Prince of Jiangxia Yigong died at nineteen, unmarried; the ritual officers deliberated adult mourning, and the princes wore great mourning.

sentences.zh: 左丞孫敻重奏：「禮記'女子十五而笄'，鄭玄云：' 應年許嫁者也。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director Sun Xuan resubmitted, "The Book of Rites says 'a girl at fifteen performs the hairpin ceremony'—Zheng Xuan says, 'the age when she should be promised in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Director Sun Xuan resubmitted: "The Book of Rites says 'a girl at fifteen performs the hairpin ceremony'—Zheng Xuan says, 'the age when she should be promised in marriage.

sentences.zh: 其未許嫁者，則二十而笄。

translations.literal: If she is not yet promised, then at twenty she performs the hairpin.
translations.idiomatic: If she is not yet promised in marriage, then at twenty she performs the hairpin.

sentences.zh: '射慈云：'十九猶為殤。

translations.literal: She Ci says, 'nineteen is still early death.
translations.idiomatic: She Ci says, 'nineteen still counts as early death.

sentences.zh: '禮官違越經典，於理無據。

translations.literal: The ritual officers violate and exceed the classics; in principle there is no basis."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officers violate and exceed the classics; in principle they have no basis."

sentences.zh: 」太常以下結免贖論，謐坐杖督五十，奪勞百日。

translations.literal: The Grand Minister of Ceremonies and those below concluded exemption by ransom; Mi was sentenced to beating with the staff fifty times and loss of merit for a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Minister of Ceremonies and those below concluded exemption by ransom; Mi was sentenced to fifty strokes of the staff and loss of merit for a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 謐又奏敻先不研辯，混同謬議，准以事例，亦宜及咎。

translations.literal: Mi again memorialized that Xuan had earlier failed to investigate and debate, mixing erroneous deliberation; according to precedent he too should bear guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Mi again memorialized that Xuan had earlier failed to investigate and debate, mixing erroneous deliberation; by precedent he too should bear guilt.

sentences.zh: 敻又結免贖論，詔可。

translations.literal: Xuan again concluded exemption by ransom; the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan again concluded exemption by ransom; the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 出為建平王景素冠軍長史、長沙內史，行湘州事。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Aide to Prince of Jianping Jingsu, Champion, Interior Administrator of Changsha, acting in Xiang Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Chief Aide to Champion Prince of Jianping Jingsu, Interior Administrator of Changsha, acting in Xiang Province affairs.

sentences.zh: 政教苛刻，僧遵道又與謐情款，隨謐蒞郡，犯小事，餓系郡獄。

translations.literal: His governance and teaching were harsh and exacting; the monk Zundao was also on intimate terms with Mi and followed Mi to the commandery; for a small offense he was starved and imprisoned in the commandery jail.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was harsh and exacting; the monk Zundao was also intimate with Mi and followed Mi to the commandery; for a small offense he was starved and imprisoned in the commandery jail.

sentences.zh: 僧遵道裂三衣食之盡而死，為有司奏，征還。

translations.literal: Zundao tore three sets of clothes and ate them until dead; the relevant offices reported it and Mi was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Zundao tore three sets of clothes and ate them until he died; the relevant offices reported it and Mi was recalled.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，遇赦免。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died he met amnesty and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Ming died he met amnesty and was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 謐才長刀筆，所在幹職。

translations.literal: Mi's talent lay in legal documents; wherever he served he handled affairs competently.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's talent lay in legal documents; wherever he served he handled affairs competently; so it ended.

sentences.zh: 高帝崩，謐稱疾不入，眾頗疑其怨不預顧命。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao died Mi claimed illness and did not enter; many suspected he resented not being included in the final commands.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Gao died Mi claimed illness and did not enter; many suspected he resented not being included in the final commands.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，謐又不遷官，以此怨望。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne Mi again did not transfer posts, and for this harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Wu took the throne Mi again did not transfer posts, and for this harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 時武帝不豫，謐詣豫章王嶷，請閑曰：「至尊非起疾，東宮又非才，公今欲何計？

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wu was ill; Mi went to Prince of Yuzhang Ni and asked leave, saying, "The Supreme One is not recovering from illness, and the Eastern Palace lacks talent—what plan does Your Highness now intend?"
translations.idiomatic: Then Emperor Wu was ill; Mi went to Prince of Yuzhang Ni and asked leave, saying, "The Supreme One is not recovering from illness, and the Eastern Palace lacks talent—what plan does Your Highness now intend?"

sentences.zh: 」武帝知之，出謐為鎮北長史、南東海太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu learned of it and sent Mi out as Chief Aide to the Pacifying North and Administrator of Eastern Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu learned of it and sent Mi out as Chief Aide to the Pacifying North and Administrator of Eastern Donghai; so it ended.

sentences.zh: 未發，憂甚，乃以奕棋占卦云：「有客南來，金碗玉杯。

translations.literal: Before he set out his anxiety was extreme; he divined by weiqi and said, "A guest comes from the south—a golden bowl and jade cup."
translations.idiomatic: Before he departed his anxiety was extreme; he cast a weiqi divination and said, "A guest comes from the south—a golden bowl and jade cup."

sentences.zh: 」上使御史中丞沈沖奏謐前後罪惡，請收送廷尉。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Censor-in-Chief Shen Chong to memorialize Mi's former and latter crimes and request arrest and delivery to the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven sent Censor-in-Chief Shen Chong to memorialize Mi's former and latter crimes and request arrest and delivery to the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 詔賜死，果以金罌盛藥鴆之。

translations.literal: An edict sentenced him to death; indeed a golden jar held the poisoned draught.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sentenced him to death; indeed a golden jar held the poisoned draught; so it ended.

sentences.zh: 子介，建武中為吳令，政亦深苛。

translations.literal: His son Jie in the Jianwu era was Magistrate of Wu; his governance was also deeply harsh.
translations.idiomatic: The subject's son Jie in the Jianwu era was Magistrate of Wu; his governance was also deeply harsh.

sentences.zh: 人間榜死人髑髏為謐首，介棄官而去。

translations.literal: People posted a dead man's skull as Mi's head; Jie abandoned office and left.
translations.idiomatic: People posted a dead man's skull as Mi's head; Jie abandoned office and left; so it ended.

sentences.zh: 論曰：敬元夷簡歸譽，玄保弘懿見推，其取重於世，豈虛名也。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Jingyuan's quiet simplicity won lasting praise, Xuanbao's steady virtue earned promotion—their weight in the world was no empty name.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary says: Jingyuan's quiet simplicity won lasting praise, Xuanbao's steady virtue earned promotion—their weight in the world was no empty name; so it ended.

sentences.zh: 然玄保時隆帝念，雖命稟于玄天，跡其恩寵，蓋亦「猶賢」之助。

translations.literal: Yet when Xuanbao enjoyed the emperor's favor at the height of the age, though fate came from the dark heaven, tracing his grace and favor, it was also the help of "still worthy."
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Xuanbao enjoyed imperial favor at the height of the age, though fate came from the dark heaven, tracing his grace and favor, it was also the help of "still worthy."

sentences.zh: 沈氏世傳武節，而演之以業尚見知，綢繆帷幄，遂參機務。

translations.literal: The Shen clan for generations transmitted martial valor, yet Yanzhi was known for upholding principle; bound closely in the tent, he shared confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Shen clan for generations transmitted martial valor, yet Yanzhi won renown for upholding principle; bound closely in the tent, he shared confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 處默保閑篤素，叔源節見臨危，懿德高風，所謂世有人矣。

translations.literal: Chumo preserved leisure and plain integrity, Shuyuan showed integrity facing peril—their lofty virtue and high bearing show that the age had its men.
translations.idiomatic: Chumo preserved leisure and plain integrity, Shuyuan showed integrity facing peril—their lofty virtue and high bearing show that the age had its men; so it ended.

sentences.zh: 茂遠自晉及陳，雅道相系，弈世載德，斯之謂焉。

translations.literal: From Jin through Chen Maoyuan's elegant way continued in succession, virtue carried generation after generation—this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin through Chen Maoyuan's elegant way continued in succession, virtue carried generation after generation—this is what is meant; so it ended.

sentences.zh: 而總溺於寵狎，反以文雅為敗，然則士之成名，所貴彬彬而已。

translations.literal: Yet Zong drowned in favor and intimacy and in the end was ruined by elegance—thus in making a name, what matters is balanced completeness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zong drowned in favor and intimacy and in the end was ruined by elegance—thus in making a name, what matters is balanced completeness; so it ended.

sentences.zh: 玄叔清介著美，足以追蹤古烈。

translations.literal: Xuanshu's purity and integrity won lasting praise, enough to follow the tracks of ancient worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanshu's purity and integrity won lasting praise, enough to follow the tracks of ancient worthies; so it ended.

sentences.zh: 令和窺覘成性，終取躓于險塗，宜矣。

translations.literal: Linghe's habit of spying and probing became his nature; in the end he stumbled on a perilous road—as was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Linghe's habit of spying and probing became his nature; in the end he stumbled on a perilous road—as was fitting; so it ended.
